best.title: Astrocytes contribute to long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism affecting microglia in fragile X syndrome.
best.abstract: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) influence membrane structure and function, energy metabolism, inflammation, and the ability to regulate microglial activity. We show involvement of astrocytes in long-chain PUFA metabolism in human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived astrocytes with fragile X syndrome (FXS). FXS astrocytes secreted more n-6 docosapentaenoic acid (n-6 DPA) and displayed a higher n-3 DPA to docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) ratio in medium than controls, consistent with an altered n-6 to n-3 PUFA balance in plasma from the FXS mouse. The FXS-specific increase in n-6 DPA secretion was abolished by treatment with all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), which affected gene expression in astrocyte subpopulations and modulated secreted triacylglycerol species. Microglial exposure to n-6 DPA stimulated expression of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which also tended to increase in microglia with reduced inflammatory marker expression when cultured in medium from ATRA-treated astrocytes. The results indicate that astrocyte-mediated n-6 DPA regulates the trophic functions of microglia in FXS.

best.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
best.abstract: BACKGROUND: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant. PURPOSE: : We aimed to refine the phenotypic spectrum associated with novel TUBGCP6 variants in 3 patients, including 2 with biallelic missense variants, and compare them with 13 previously reported cases. METHODS: : Neurological, cognitive, and neuroimaging data were assessed in 3 patients carrying TUBGCP6 variants identified using next-generation sequencing. These 3 patients were recruited through the Microfanc project (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01565005) or a call for collaboration with the ITHACA European Reference Network. Functional analyses of the fibroblasts from 1 patient included Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and proximity ligation assays. Variants were further characterized using complementary sequence- and structure-based in silico analyses, including structural modeling, stability, conservation, and protein language model-based predictions. RESULTS: : None of the patients had chorioretinopathy or short stature at the last follow-up (age: 7.8, 15, and 17.6 years). Two patients presented with malformations of cortical development, microcephaly, gyral simplification, and focal epilepsy. Cognitive impairment ranged from borderline intelligence quotient to severe ID. Patient 1 carried compound heterozygous missense variants, p.(Val359Ile) and p.(Gly990Arg). TUBGCP6 failed to localize to the centrosome and to interact with γ-tubulin. Patient 2 carried the homozygous missense variant p.(Leu448Pro) predicted to destabilize TUBGCP6. Patient 3 harbored 2 compound heterozygous frameshift variants, p.(Gln1389GlyfsTer13), which was predicted to under gononsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD), and p.(Pro1759AlafsTer68), which may produce an aberrant C-terminal extension, although NMD remains possible. CONCLUSION: : This study expands the phenotypic spectrum of TUBGCP6-related diseases to include malformations of cortical development, microcephaly with or without ID, and the absence of chorioretinopathy. Our combined in vitro and in silico findings suggest that stable but dysfunctional TUBGCP6 may produce a more severe brain phenotype than a complete loss of function, while sparing the retina. However, these mechanistic insights remain preliminary.

best.title: Gut microbiota profiles and neurodevelopmental symptoms in children from a prenatal-risk enriched birth cohort: findings from the PREDO study.
best.abstract: BACKGROUND: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) are common neurodevelopmental conditions whose early-life biological correlates remain incompletely understood. Children's gut microbiota may represent a biological pathway through which immune-metabolic and gut-brain signalling links early-life adversity with neurodevelopment. We examined gut microbiota profiles associated with ADHD and ASD symptoms in children from the Prediction and Prevention of Preeclampsia and Intrauterine Growth Restriction (PREDO) birth cohort. METHODS: We analysed data from 323 Finnish children assessed at a mean age of 8.6 years. Stool microbiota composition was profiled using 16S rRNA sequencing and differential taxonomic abundance was assessed using MaAsLin2. ADHD and ASD symptoms were mother-rated using the Conners' Parent Rating Scale-Revised and Autism Spectrum Screening Questionnaire. RESULTS: Clinically relevant ADHD and ASD symptoms were associated with metric-specific reductions in alpha diversity, whereas beta diversity did not differ between groups. Male children with clinically relevant ADHD symptoms showed lower abundance of Lachnospiraceae_FCS020_group, Subdoligranulum, Fusicatenibacter, and Anaerostipes (ps ≤ 0.049). Female children with clinically relevant ADHD symptoms showed a distinct profile, including higher Negativibacillus and Faecalibacterium (p ≤ 0.018). Children with clinically relevant ASD symptoms showed lower abundance of six genera, including Anaerostipes and Lachnospiraceae_ND3007_group (p ≤ 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this prenatal-risk enriched cohort, ADHD and ASD symptoms were associated with distinct gut microbiota profiles, including alterations in taxa implicated in short-chain fatty acid metabolism, immune regulation, and gut-brain signalling. These findings support microbiota-immune-brain pathways as a hypothesis-generating framework for future longitudinal and multi-omics research.

best.title: Proteomic Analysis of Plasma Small Extracellular Vesicles and Targeted Metabolomic Analysis of Plasma From Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
best.abstract: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder with deficits in social communication and interaction, restricted and repetitive behaviors, and unusual stereotyped interests or activities. With a lack of molecular information on the etiology of ASD, early diagnosis of this disease remains a challenge. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), as extracellular vesicles containing various important biomolecules, have been demonstrated to have a functional impact on physiological processes in the central nervous system. Herein, we profiled the proteome of plasma sEVs collected from preschool children with autism and performed targeted metabolic analysis on their plasma samples. Screening of the differentiated proteins between autistic and healthy children revealed potential biomarkers, including those involved in calcium ion binding, such as MACF1 and CALM3. Bioinformatic investigation further identified 10 outlier proteins, such as EHD1 and ERF3A, strongly associated with autism. Targeted metabolic analysis and IPA prediction suggested the potential involvement of the PI3K-AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. The sEV proteomic and plasma metabolomic analyses were performed in parallel, and pathway-level findings from each dataset were compared descriptively. These results provide insight into the biological mechanism of autism and promise in determining biomarkers for the early diagnosis of ASD. best.title: Decolonising Autistic Phenomenology: Towards a Critical-Enactive Account of Cognitive Diversity.
best.abstract: Recent years have seen a turn toward phenomenological, ecological, and enactive approaches to autism and neurodiversity, within the philosophy of psychiatry and cognitive science. These approaches challenge dominant neuro-reductionist and computational biomedical paradigms, centring embodiment, relationality, affectivity, and the constitutive role of sociomaterial environments in cognition. However, both phenomenological and ecological-enactive approaches are heterogeneous; not all escape the Eurocentric neuronormative assumptions underlying colonial modernity. This paper argues that, where classical phenomenology positions autism as a deviation from implicitly Western standards of 'neurotypical' embodiment and intersubjectivity, critical phenomenology and enactivism supply promising resources to reconceive autistic traits as intrinsically meaningful forms of sense-making - whilst interrogating the universality of categories such as 'autism' and 'neurotypicality.' Critical phenomenology draws attention to how power shapes embodiment, stretching the phenomenological method to confront its own complicity in Eurocentric neuronormativity. Enactivism goes further, providing an inclusive relational ontology of cognitive diversity that can facilitate dialogue with non-Western and Indigenous ways of knowing. Yet it risks becoming politically neutralised when inattentive to coloniality and intersectional oppression. Drawing insight from South Asian autistic experiences, I sketch out a critical-enactive framework oriented toward dismantling both neuronormative and Eurocentric (including logocentric and anthropocentric) assumptions in phenomenology and cognitive science. This decolonial approach paves the way for a pluralistic, intercultural understanding of autism - and embodied cognitive diversity, more broadly - doing justice to culturally and ecologically situated styles of sense-making, without essentialising neurological or cognitive differences.

best.title: WFS1 deficiency impacts GnRH neuron development through mechanisms involving ER stress dysregulation.
best.abstract: Wolfram Syndrome, a rare neurodegenerative disorder caused by biallelic mutations in the WFS1 gene, presents with endocrine and neurological features. Although hypogonadism has been described in Wolfram Syndrome, the role of WFS1 in reproductive development is not well understood. Congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by deficient development or function of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons. Through whole-exome sequencing in familial CHH cases, we identified two rare heterozygous missense variants in WFS1. Functional in vitro assays revealed reduced protein levels, activation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and unfolded protein response (UPR). Zebrafish and mouse embryos studies showed WFS1 expression in regions critical for GnRH neuron development. Knockdown of wfs1b in Tg(GnRH3:EGFP) zebrafish embryos disrupted GnRH3 neuronal architecture and downregulated isl1a, a key transcription factor for axon guidance. Our findings support a mechanistic model linking WFS1-mediated ER homeostasis, isl1a expression, and GnRH neuron development. We propose WFS1 as a novel candidate modifier in CHH pathogenesis and provide in vivo evidence that ER stress and isl1a dysregulation impair the formation of GnRH neuronal network.

best.title: Subfield-specific hippocampal enlargement in high-functioning autism spectrum disorder.
best.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although previous studies have reported abnormal hippocampal volumes in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), the specific alterations in hippocampal subfields and their relationships with clinical symptoms in high-functioning ASD (HF-ASD) remain unclear. METHODS: In this study, we analyzed T1-weighted structural MRI data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE-I), including 182 children and adolescents with HF-ASD and 213 age- and sex-matched typically developing controls (TDC). Using a linear mixed-effects model, we compared hippocampal volumes between groups, and examined associations between volumes and clinical measurements. RESULTS: Compared to TDC, the children and adolescents with HF-ASD exhibited significantly increased volumes in the right entire hippocampus, presubiculum, subiculum, and granule cell layer of the dentate gyrus (GC-DG). No significant volumetric differences were observed within the child or adolescent subgroups, nor between these age groups. Notably, presubiculum volume showed a positive correlation with verbal scores and a negative correlation with social scores in the HF-ASD group. CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate subfield-specific hippocampal overgrowth in children and adolescents with HF-ASD and presubiculum volume alteration may be a potential neuroanatomical correlate underlying verbal and social dysfunctions.

best.abstract: This study sought to examine the direct effects of puberty on dual systems imbalance for male and female youth and test for a moderating effect of autism spectrum disorder. Findings suggest the importance of autism and potentially pubertal developmental rate for understanding dual systems development for male youth, but not female youth.

best.title: Associations of Blood Metal(loid) Mixture with Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: A Case-Control Study.
best.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder influenced by both genetic susceptibility and environmental exposures. Heavy metals and metalloids can cross the blood-brain barrier and disturb neurodevelopment; however, most previous studies focused on single-metal effects rather than real-world mixed co-exposure. This case-control study aimed to evaluate associations between blood metal(loid) mixtures and childhood ASD risk. 30 children with ASD and 30 typically-developing controls aged 2-7 years were enrolled in Guangxi, China. Whole-blood concentrations of lead, mercury, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, and manganese were measured by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Univariate analyses, multivariable logistic regression, and quantile-based g-computation (qgcomp) were applied to assess individual and joint effects. Univariate results showed higher blood lead and cadmium concentrations in ASD children. After adjusting for covariates, each doubling of blood cadmium concentration was associated with higher odds of ASD (Firth-penalized OR = 18.64, 95% CI: 1.75-315.18; P = 0.014); the maximum-likelihood estimate was similar in direction but wider (OR = 27.96, 95% CI: 2.20-577.77; P = 0.017). Because of the small number of events this estimate is interpreted with caution. In the qgcomp model, a simultaneous one-quartile increase in all six metal(loid)s was associated with higher odds of ASD, although the joint effect was not statistically significant (OR = 1.28, 95% CI: 0.70-2.35; P = 0.422). Cadmium carried the largest positive weight within the mixture (0.43), and manganese the largest negative weight (- 0.31); because the weights are constrained to sum to unity in absolute value and the joint effect was not significant, they are interpreted as descriptive summaries of relative contribution rather than as tests of the effect of each metal(loid). Our findings suggest that blood cadmium concentration may be associated with ASD, but the evidence is limited: the joint effect of the mixture was not statistically significant, the component weights are descriptive rather than tests of individual effects, and the single-metal estimate for cadmium was imprecise. These observations highlight the necessity of mixture-exposure assessment in ASD-related environmental epidemiological research, and require replication in larger samples.

best.title: Genomic landscape of rare variants in a Chinese autism cohort and discovery of novel risk genes.
best.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a genetically complex neurodevelopmental condition with a high heritability. However, genomic studies of ASD have been underrepresented in East Asian populations, and the molecular yield in ASD cohorts remains modest. Here, we present a whole-genome sequencing analysis of 3109 samples across 1033 Chinese ASD families. By examining a wide spectrum of genetic variation, we identified rare ASD-associated variants in 19.2% of affected individuals, providing a population-specific view of the genetic architecture of ASD. We identify significant enrichment of de novo variants in probands, nominate or strengthen candidate risk genes (e.g., NCL, SPPL3, ADGRB1, SLC9A3, KIF1B) through mutational burden, evolutionary constraint, recurrent missense site, and functional assays, and implicate convergent pathways including protein palmitoylation. By integrating over 40,000 ASD cases across unpublished and published global cohorts, we identify 245 ASD risk genes, including 45 with limited prior evidence and 32 with no prior association. Single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the developing human cortex reveals that ASD risk genes exhibit widespread yet heterogeneous expression across all major cell types, with peak expression in excitatory neurons, particularly intratelencephalic neurons, and enriched expression in microglia (e.g., C1QC, CARD11, SNX13, MEF2C, FOXP2, TCF12, MED13L), suggesting convergent involvement of both synaptic and neuroimmune mechanisms. Together, our findings expand the ASD genetic landscape and suggest convergent pathogenic axes involving transcriptional regulation, synaptic signaling and plasticity, and neuroimmune interactions. This work supports the development of inclusive diagnostic strategies and provides a foundation for mechanistic and intervention exploration in ASD.

best.title: Disruption of dynactin complex function in intellectual disability.
best.abstract: Intellectual disability (ID) is a highly prevalent condition affecting approximately 200 millions of people worldwide, characterized by impaired cognitive function. Dynactin complex consists of multiple protein subunits and is required for intracellular trafficking and synaptic homeostasis in developing and mature neurons. Here, we identify deleterious variants of dynactin subunit 4 (DCTN4) in ID pedigrees. DCTN4 ablation in mice results in altered neuronal positioning and apoptosis in neural progenitor cells. Notably, mice carrying the ID-linked DCTN4 variant exhibit cognitive deficits with impaired dendritic development. Cortical neurons with DCTN4 deficiency or variant show reduced levels of various dynactin subunits, suggesting that deficits in dynactin complex affects synaptic function. Furthermore, disruption of the DCTN4-JIP3 complex impairs lysosomal transport and dendritic development as well as synaptic development. Importantly, we showed that damaging variants in another dynactin subunit DCTN2 also disrupt neuronal positioning, reinforcing the critical role of dynactin complex in neurodevelopment and ID pathogenesis. These findings illustrate dysfunctional dynactin complex as a previously unrecognized disease mechanism of ID.

best.title: Perspectives of parents of children with monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders on research involving patient-derived neuronal models.
best.abstract: Patient-derived stem cell-based neuronal models hold great promise for advancing research into monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders (mNDDs). These neuronal models are generated using induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technologies, and are perceived as "ethically sensitive". To date, ethical discussions on the use of neuronal models have predominantly focused on three-dimensional (3D) neuronal models, such as brain organoids, while two-dimensional (2D) neuronal models - which are widely used in current research settings - remain underexplored. A better understanding of the perspectives of parents of children with mNDDs on ethical issues - including the moral status of 2D models, informed consent, autonomy, privacy and misuse - is needed. We report the results of a semi-structured interview study among parents of children with mNDDs (n = 28) investigating their perspectives on the ethically responsible use of 2D patient-derived neuronal models in research. Respondents ascribed limited intrinsic value to neuronal models, often viewing them as ethically comparable to other somatic cells. They were highly motivated to enroll their child in iPSC research, but suggested that researchers: (1) restrict the use of their child's donated material to purposes benefiting the mNDD community, (2) protect their child's privacy, (3) communicate about research findings and reuse of donated material, and (4) minimize risks and burdens of research procedures for their (vulnerable) child. Based on these findings, we provide recommendations to research groups for informed consent and engagement processes to support responsible inclusion of children with mNDDs and their families in research using iPSC-based neuronal models.

best.title: International Multicenter Retrospective Study on UBTF-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
best.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: UBTF encodes the upstream binding transcription factor (UBTF), a protein essential for rRNA synthesis. Dominantly acting pathogenic variants, either de novo or inherited, have been associated with a broad clinical childhood-onset neurodegenerative/neurodevelopmental spectrum whose genotype-phenotype correlation has not been accurately defined yet. This multicenter study aims to conduct a retrospective analysis of a large cohort of patients with pathogenic variants in the UBTF gene to refine diagnostic criteria and identify clinically relevant outcome measures for future trials. METHODS: Clinical centers provided clinical, molecular, and neuroimaging data on patients carrying pathogenic or predicted pathogenic UBTF variants, consistent with the clinical phenotype. Data were collected using an human phenotype ontology-based standardized electronic case report form and included unreported cases or updated information on patients reported in the literature from January 2017 to December 2024. RESULTS: A cohort of 49 patients (23 previously unreported) was included in the study. The disease typically presented at ≤3 years (89.6%) with neuroregression in 71.4% of cases, either in a child with preexisting neurodevelopmental delay (42.9%) or after previously normal psychomotor development (28.6%). Less frequently, neurodevelopmental delay occurred in isolation (26.5%). During disease progression, patients developed behavioral abnormalities (81.6%), movement disorders (78.3%), autonomic manifestations (50.0%), and epilepsy (34.7%). At the last follow-up (mean age 13 years and 6 months), only 2 patients were deceased (4.1%). The main neuroimaging findings included white matter hyperintensity (68.1%), cerebral (66.0%) and cerebellar (51.1%) atrophy, and thinning of the corpus callosum (38.3%). However, brain MRI findings were reported as normal in 21.3% of cases. We identified 7 novel UBTF variants (c.271G>C; c.349A>T; c.495C>A; c.517G>A; c.761A>G; c.1048-2A>G; and c.1625_1626+15del). Genotype-phenotype analysis led to the distinction of 2 allelic, clinically distinct disorders: a childhood-onset neurodegenerative disease due to gain-of-function variants, characterized by the triad of neuroregression, movement, and behavioral disorders, and a neurodevelopmental disorder with a milder clinical course associated with loss-of-function/hypomorphic variants. DISCUSSION: The results from our deep-phenotyping analysis suggest the classification of UBTF-related disease into 2 main clinical syndromes impacting the natural history of the disease with a different degree of severity and complexity. This novel observation should be considered in the management and prognosis of patients and will be fundamental in the design of targeted therapies.

best.title: Cross-tissue transcriptome-wide association analyses prioritize the 17q21.31 locus in autism spectrum disorder.
best.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has a complex genetic architecture, and the regulatory transcripts underlying common-variant associations with ASD risks remain incompletely resolved. We integrated ASD genome-wide association summary statistics with genetically predicted expression across 29 GTEx v8 tissues using Joint-Tissue Imputation (JTI) and FUSION, followed by summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), regional conditional/joint analysis, colocalization and comparison with external ASD molecular evidence. All-tissue false-discovery-rate correction identified 264 significant JTI gene-tissue associations representing 64 genes and 561 FUSION associations representing 128 genes, with an overlap of 40 genes between JTI and FUSION and 152 unique genes in the union set. Brain eQTL and mQTL SMR identified 22 and 21 significant probes, respectively, while analyses across 16 non-brain tissues identified 59 significant probe-tissue associations. TWAS signals converged at 17q21.31. Conditional/joint FUSION retained only the Brain Cerebellar Hemisphere MAPT-AS1 model among 353 significant associations in the primary regional analysis, with the same model retained in an extended-window sensitivity analysis. BrainMeta-ASD colocalization was completed for 23 probes; none met the prespecified criterion for strong colocalization, and MAPT showed the highest PP·H4 (0.5052). Among the 152 union genes, 82 were supported by at least one of the Huang, Matoba or Gandal studies and 15 by at least two; MAPT and XRN2 were the only genes supported by all three data sets. MAPT-AS1 was supported by Matoba et al. in H-MAGMA analysis and is classified as a Category 2 gene in SFARI Gene, while Walker et al. provided additional developmental-brain context through prenatal-brain TWAS. These findings prioritize 17q21.31 as an ASD-associated locus supported across multiple genetic and regulatory evidence layers.

best.title: Disruption of GAD1 protein architecture by a novel missense variant in a consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability.
best.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intellectual disability represents a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders marked by significant impairments in intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior. Among the various causes, genetic factors play a major role, with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID) constituting a genetically diverse subgroup. ARID is prevalent in consanguineous families and arises from homozygous mutations that disrupt critical genes involved in brain development and function. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify disease-causing genetic variants responsible for ARID in a consanguineous Pakistani family and to evaluate the structural and functional impact of a novel variant identified in GAD1 through protein modeling. METHODS: A consanguineous family affected with intellectual disability was enrolled. Whole-exome sequencing was performed on an affected individual, followed by bioinformatics analysis including alignment to the GRCh38 reference genome, variant calling, and annotation. Variants were filtered based on rarity, predicted functional impact, and autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. Candidate variants were validated and assessed by Sanger sequencing and segregation analysis. Protein modeling was performed to evaluate the structural impact of the identified variant. RESULTS: A novel homozygous missense variant NM_000817:c.1700G>A;p.Arg567Gln in GAD1 was identified. Segregation analysis confirmed co-segregation of the variant with the affected phenotype. Protein modeling suggested that the variant may disrupt GAD1 enzymatic function involved in gamma-aminobutyric acid synthesis. CONCLUSION: This study emphasizes the significance of genetic investigation in familial cases and the crucial role that GAD1 mutations play in neurodevelopmental disorders with intellectual disability. The results advance the knowledge of molecular causes of ARID and broaden the mutational range.

best.title: Overexpression of endoplasmic reticulum acetyl-CoA transporter AT-1 alters neuronal metabolism, growth, and synaptic activity.
best.abstract: Acetyl-CoA is a molecule central to cellular metabolic homeostasis. As part of the secretory pathway, acetyl-CoA is imported into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) by a membrane-bound transporter AT-1 (SLC33A1). AT-1 mutations have been linked to peripheral neuropathy, developmental delay with premature death, and intellectual disability with progeria. Here, we show that AT-1 overexpression impacts diverse phenotypes related to neuronal function and plasticity. Differences in ribosomal, synaptic processing, and metabolic pathways were identified at transcriptomic and proteomic levels. Metabolic adaptations included changes in mitochondrial membrane potential, architecture, and respiration, and tracing experiments revealed changes in the fate of glucose favoring glycogen storage over the pentose phosphate pathway. Altered redox was linked to NAD-dependent proteins SIRT1 and CtBP2. Depletion of lipid stores was associated with greater plasticity in fuel substrate utilization. Metabolic adaptation was coincident with decreased synaptic activity, indicating that neuronal communication is coordinated, in part, through acetyl-CoA metabolism.

best.title: Stress-induced alterations in neurodevelopment in iPSC-Derived i n vitro model systems.
best.abstract: Psychological stress is common in women during pregnancy and after childbirth, showing a prevalence of up to 15.6% in pregnant women in developing countries. Clinical and pre-clinical studies have implicated their role in negatively affecting pregnancy outcomes and have been linked to adverse child outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, specifically the signatures associated with their effect on human fetal development. Thereby, impairing our further understanding of the effects of therapeutics used to treat these disorders in expecting mothers. This study proposes the use of human iPSC-derived embryoid bodies (EBs) and forebrain-specific organoids as complementary human developmental models to investigate the effects of exposure to prenatal stress (mediated by glucocorticoids) across distinct stages, in vitro. Our findings suggested that excessive glucocorticoids altered early lineage specification in an exposure-dependent manner. This was evidenced by a brief increase in pluripotent and neural progenitor populations, with mild alterations in proliferative dynamics without a net change in proliferative capacity. Changes in lineage-associated markers were observed in ectodermal and meso-endodermal layers of EBs. Particularly, focusing on neurogenesis (forebrain-specific organoids) to understand the impact of stress on neurodevelopment, we saw concentration-dependent changes in progenitor maintenance and neuronal- glial differentiation. Furthermore, the activation of inflammatory and oxidative stress responses can be implicated as signalling mechanisms responsible for the differences observed. Together, these results suggest that glucocorticoid signalling linked to prenatal stress can alter developmental trajectories by modifying cellular states rather than directly altering proliferation or survival during early development.

best.title: Persistent autism-like behaviors and multilevel neurobiological abnormalities following prenatal valproic acid exposure in rats.
best.abstract: Prenatal valproic acid (VPA) exposure is widely used to model autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the persistence of its behavioral effects and the accompanying multilevel neurobiological abnormalities remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated behavioral, histological, morphological, electrophysiological, molecular, metabolomic, and epigenomic analyses to characterize the long-term effects of prenatal VPA exposure in rats from early postnatal life through adulthood. Prenatal VPA exposure caused delayed early development and persistent ASD-like phenotypes, including repetitive behaviors, impaired social interaction, anxiety-like behavior, reduced exploration, and cognitive deficits. These behavioral abnormalities were accompanied by neuronal and glial alterations and reduced dendritic complexity and spine density in the medial prefrontal cortex and hippocampus, as well as reduced excitatory and inhibitory synaptic inputs and decreased expression of key synaptic proteins in the medial prefrontal cortex. Multi-omics profiling further identified candidate metabolic alterations involving membrane lipid remodeling, neuromodulatory metabolism, and inflammatory lipid signaling, alongside bidirectional, locus-specific DNA methylation changes enriched in neurodevelopmental and synaptic pathways. Together, these findings show that prenatal VPA exposure produces persistent ASD-like phenotypes accompanied by multilevel cellular, structural, synaptic, metabolic, and epigenetic abnormalities. This work provides an integrated framework for understanding the long-term consequences of prenatal VPA exposure and supports the VPA model as a valuable platform for investigating mechanisms underlying ASD.

best.title: Deep Brain Stimulation of the Nucleus Accumbens and Anterior Limb of the Internal Capsule in Severe Autism Spectrum Disorder: Clinical Outcomes and Infralimbic-Accumbens Circuit Involvement.
best.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder with limited effective treatments. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has emerged as a potential intervention, yet its efficacy and mechanisms remain poorly understood. We conducted a prospective, single-arm cohort study of nucleus accumbens-anterior limb of the internal capsule (NAc-ALIC) DBS in patients with severe ASD, observing preliminary safety and longitudinal reductions in repetitive-behaviour and social-domain symptom severity during follow-up. Exploratory sweet-spot analysis suggested a candidate medial-ventral NAc region associated with social-domain score reductions. In a maternal immune activation mouse model, NAc-DBS enhanced social novelty preference and reduced repetitive behaviours. NAc-DBS partially normalized aberrant oscillatory activity in the NAc and infralimbic cortex (IL), increased IL neuronal activity, and enhanced cross-frequency coupling. Chemogenetic activation of the IL→NAc projection enhanced social novelty preference, whereas inhibition of IL neurons projecting to the NAc attenuated the DBS-associated social novelty improvement without affecting marble-burying behaviour. NAc-DBS also increased glutamate, AMPA receptor, and brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels, consistent with enhanced synaptic plasticity. Together, these findings provide exploratory clinical evidence of longitudinal reductions in symptom severity during follow-up after NAc-ALIC DBS and suggest that NAc stimulation modulates IL and NAc neural activity, implicates the IL→NAc pathway, and engages plasticity-related processes.

best.title: Maternal gluten diet exacerbates offspring autistic-like behaviors through the gut-brain axis mediated by gut microbial metabolite elaidic acid.
best.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by social deficits and stereotyped behaviors, for which effective treatments remain lacking. Here we investigated whether early-life gluten exposure exacerbates autism-like behaviors in BTBR mice and explored the underlying microbiota-metabolite-brain mechanism. Early-life gluten exposure aggravated social avoidance, anxiety, and repetitive behaviors in BTBR offspring, accompanied by reduced mushroom dendritic spine density and diminished microglial branch complexity in the hippocampus. Microbiota sequencing revealed gut microbial dysbiosis, with increased abundance of Hungatella hathewayi and Eubacterium sp. Marseille-P4003. Consistent with their capacity for lipid transformation, untargeted metabolomics showed enrichment of unsaturated fatty acid metabolism and elevated fecal elaidic acid levels. Clinically, targeted quantification confirmed that fecal elaidic acid was significantly higher in children with ASD than in their healthy siblings. Supporting a causal role, exogenous elaidic acid administration dose-dependently worsened behavioral deficits and induced hippocampal spine loss and amoeboid microglial activation. Mechanistically, intestinal transcriptomics revealed activation of antigen processing and presentation and cytokine signaling pathways, whereas hippocampal transcriptomics showed downregulation of immune negative regulators (Egr2, Egr4) alongside enrichment of MHC-I and TNF pathways, indicating impaired central immune restraint. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that early-life gluten exposure induces gut microbiota dysbiosis that drives elaidic acid accumulation, which in turn activates intestinal immunity and suppresses hippocampal immune negative regulation via the gut-brain axis, ultimately aggravating neuroinflammation and autism-like behaviors.

best.title: Differential frontostriatal ΔFosB dynamics and behavioral flexibility in autism like VPA-exposed mice.
best.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves social impairments, repetitive behaviors, and behavioral inflexibility, defined as an inability to adapt behavior to changing contingencies, and is linked to frontostriatal dysfunction. How behavioral training modulates these circuits is unclear, but ΔFosB, a marker of sustained neural activity, may be useful to establish their relationship. The aim was to evaluate frontostriatal ΔFosB expression following prenatal exposure to valproic acid (VPA) and to determine how experience in the midsession reversal (MSR) task modulates posterior ΔFosB expression. CD-1 mice were prenatally exposed to VPA (500 mg/kg) or vehicle. Brains from postnatal day (PND) 30 mice were analyzed to quantify baseline ΔFosB + cells in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), dorsal striatum (DS), and ventral striatum (VS). In the second experiment, mice performed the MSR task for 13 days. Then, ΔFosB was re-evaluated at PND43 to assess experience-dependent changes. At PND30, VPA-exposed mice showed a significant increase in ΔFosB + cells in mPFC, OFC, DS, and VS, suggesting sustained activity-dependent engagement of the frontostriatal circuit. In the MSR task, mice adapted to contingency shifts using mixed strategies, including win-stay/lose-shift behavior and temporal estimation, whereas VPA mice showed less consistent strategy selection after reversal. After MSR, ΔFosB expression in the OFC and striatum of VPA mice normalized to control levels and remained persistently elevated in the mPFC at PND43. Thus, prenatal VPA induces long-term increases in neuronal transcriptional changes, suggesting activity-dependent plasticity in the frontostriatal circuit. Despite these neural alterations, behavioral flexibility was preserved, suggesting circuit-level adaptations underlying ASD-related strategies. Future studies could broaden these results by examining sex differences and characterizing the cellular and molecular changes dependent on frontostriatal ΔFosB dynamics.

primary.title: ALS-linked FUS mutation impairs GEMIN5-dependent mRNA recruitment to neuronal late endosomes.
primary.abstract: Neurons depend on tightly regulated positioning of cellular components to maintain long-distance signaling, but the mechanisms guiding specific mRNAs to distant regions remain unclear. Here, we show that late endosomes function as selective RNA carriers in human motor neurons and uncover the molecular logic guiding their loading. Using APEX2-mediated proximity labeling, we identify the external transcriptome of RAB7A-positive endosomes and find a specific population of mRNAs enriched for endosomal, axonal, and synaptic functions. We find that mRNAs enriched in RAB7A endosomes contain evolutionarily conserved 5'UTRs that act as localization signals, and that the RNA-binding protein GEMIN5 interacts with these regions to promote endosomal RNA recruitment. Finally, we show that there is a conspicuous loss of endosome-associated transcripts in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-associated conditions, accompanied by the mislocalization of GEMIN5 from endosomes. These findings uncover fundamental principles of RNA compartmentalization and highlight endosomal mRNA loading as a vulnerable axis in neuronal homeostasis.

primary.title: Galectin-3 links microglial neuroinflammation to Aβ aggregation and lysosomal processing.
primary.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify galectin-3 (Gal3) as a regulator of plaque-associated microglial responses, linking Aβ aggregation, lysosomal function, and neuritic pathology. Using postmortem brain tissue from AD patients, we found that Gal3+ microglia preferentially associate with cored plaques and correlate with increased LAMP1+ dystrophic neurites. Gal3 was also detected in microglial lysosomal compartments, extramicroglial dystrophic structures, and in association with extracellular amyloid fibrils, suggesting roles in both intracellular and extracellular Aβ processing. In APP mice, Gal3 deficiency reduced plaque burden and neuritic dystrophy, increased plaque compaction, and enhanced TREM2 coverage around amyloid plaques. Mechanistically, in vitro microglial experiments showed that Gal3 modulates Aβ uptake and lysosomal processing, whereas lysosomal dysfunction promoted the accumulation of fibrillar Aβ from initially monomeric species, particularly in Gal3-deficient cells. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Gal3 preferentially binds fibrillar Aβ, inhibits secondary nucleation, and alters fibril morphology, while Gal3-modified fibrillar Aβ reduces N2a neuronal cell number. Finally, in silico structural analyses identified candidate Gal3 interactors enriched in leucine-rich-repeat and immunoglobulin-like proteins, supporting a role for this lectin in immune receptor regulation. Complementary in vivo transcriptomic profiling showed that Gal3 deletion suppresses type I interferon and microglial neurodegenerative transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings position Gal3 at the interface between Aβ remodeling, lysosomal homeostasis, and plaque-associated microglial responses in AD.

primary.title: Structural basis for the selective inhibition of the PI3KC3-C2 complex by Rubicon in endolysosome maturation and mitophagy.
primary.abstract: Rubicon is a negative regulator of autophagy and the endolysosomal network (ELN) and an antagonist of the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex II (PI3KC3-C2). Inhibition of Rubicon is considered a potential means to therapeutically upregulate autophagy and the ELN to treat Parkinson's disease and other conditions characterized by autophagic and ELN dysfunction. Rubicon is specific for the UV radiation resistance-associated gene protein (UVRAG)-containing PI3KC3-C2 over the purely autophagic ATG14-containing PI3KC3-C1 complex. Here, we determined the high-resolution cryoelectron microscopy structure of PI3KC3-C2 in complex with the PI3KC3-binding domain of Rubicon and compared it to cryo-EM structures of unbound PI3KC3-C2 and PI3KC3-C1. Rubicon binds directly to PI3KC3-C2 only via the BARA domain of the BECN1 subunit, which is common to both C1 and C2. The selectivity of Rubicon for the PI3KC3-C2 complex over the PI3KC3-C1 complex is attributed to a conformation of the BECN1BARA domain induced by UVRAG, rather than to direct contact with UVRAG or direct antagonism by the ATG14 subunit of PI3KC3-C1. Targeted disruption of the Rubicon:PI3K3-C2 structural interface by site-directed mutations enhances mitophagic activity in human epithelial cells to levels comparable to those observed in Rubicon knockout cells. Similarly, disruption of the interaction in Rubicon-overexpressing hippocampal neurons restored lysosomal flux to wild-type levels. These data show that suppressing the function of PI3K3-C2 can fully account for the negative regulatory effects of Rubicon in the autophagy and ELN pathways.

primary.title: A Cilia-Centered Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD+) Signaling Network Regulates Hypothalamic Lysosomal Homeostasis and Metabolic Aging.
primary.abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is an essential metabolite that regulates diverse cellular metabolic processes. Primary cilia, hair-like organelles on the cell surface, function as critical signaling hubs. Here, we demonstrate that cellular NAD+ levels are key regulators of both primary cilia growth and lysosomal function in hypothalamic neurons. NAD+ depletion induces ciliary shortening and diminishes lysosomal activity in a cilia-dependent manner. Mechanistically, the lysosomal repair complex protein CHMP4B translocates from periciliary satellites to lysosomes during lysosomal stress, a process impaired by ciliary dysgenesis. Disrupted lysosomal recruitment of CHMP4B leads to abnormal lysosomal Ca2+ signaling and lysosomal dysfunction. Aged mice with hypothalamic NAD+ deficiency exhibit shortened cilia and lysosomal stress phenotypes, both of which are restored by calorie restriction (CR). Moreover, CR improves aging-associated metabolic dysfunction, at least in part, through hypothalamic cilia-dependent mechanisms. These findings identify a primary cilium-mediated-NAD+ signaling axis that maintains lysosomal homeostasis in hypothalamic neurons, the disruption of which drives metabolic aging.

primary.title: Astrocytic cathepsin D promotes α-synuclein processing and Lewy neurite-like aggregate maturation.
primary.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) and related synucleinopathies are marked by the accumulation and propagation of α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregates, a process primarily studied in neurons. Whether astrocytes actively contribute to α-syn processing and intercellular transfer remains unclear. Here, using a physiologically relevant neuron-astrocyte co-culture system that recapitulates tripartite synapse architecture, we show that astrocytes process α-syn and influence the morphological maturation of neuronal aggregates. Astrocytes internalize α-syn pre-formed fibrils (PFFs) and generate C-terminally truncated α-syn species via a Cathepsin D (CtsD)-dependent process. PFF-loaded astrocytes transfer α-syn-containing material to neurons and promote the formation and maturation of pS129-α-syn-positive Lewy neurite (LN)-like aggregates. Notably, α-syn PFF exposure induces lysosomal membrane damage, a senescence-like reactive state, and CtsD upregulation in astrocytes. Although PFF-containing lysosomes undergo autophagic engulfment, they persist within astrocytes, and a subset is detected beyond the astrocytic membrane boundary. Together, our findings support a model in which astrocytic lysosomal remodeling of internalized α-syn contributes to the morphological maturation and intercellular propagation of neuronal α-syn pathology in this co-culture system.

primary.title: Ultrastructural studies reveal a new role for JIP3/MAPK8IP3 in endo-lysosomal maturation within the neuronal cell body.
primary.abstract: In recent years, substantial heterogeneity in lysosomes, in terms of their composition, function, and positioning, has come to be recognized. Despite this, there are gaps in knowledge of our understanding of the molecular basis of lysosome heterogeneity, especially in neurons. To this end, we used electron microscopy to define endolysosomal organelles of human iPSC-derived neurons at the ultrastructural level. Through this, we identify endolysosomal maturation defects within neuronal cell bodies of iNeurons lacking JNK-Interacting Protein 3 (JIP3), a lysosome adaptor previously known to primarily regulate axonal lysosome movement. Loss of JIP3 results in an expansion of immature lysosomes within neuronal soma, along with a concomitant decrease in mature lysosomes. JIP3 loss also leads to delayed trafficking of endocytic cargo through these compartments, implicating JIP3 in the regulation of endolysosomal maturation within neuronal cell bodies. Our studies highlight the utility of electron microscopy in understanding neuronal lysosomal heterogeneity. Additionally, given recent links between JIP3 and a neurodevelopmental disorder, our findings here could provide new insight into mechanisms underlying neurodevelopmental pathology.

primary.title: Isozyme-Specific Inhibition of GSK-3 Reveals Distinct Cellular Responses in Huntington's Disease Fibroblasts.
primary.abstract: Inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3) has been implicated in alleviating Huntington's disease (HD)-associated phenotypes. However, the mechanisms linking GSK-3 to HD pathogenesis, and particularly the distinct roles of GSK-3 isozymes in regulating HD-associated cellular dysfunction, remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the cellular responses of patient-derived HD fibroblasts to selective inhibition of GSK-3α or GSK-3β using isozyme-specific inhibitors, focusing on metabolic and bioenergetic pathways. Although inhibition of either isozyme suppressed mTORC1 signaling, selective GSK-3β inhibition elicited broader cellular responses, including altered oxidative stress signaling, increased expression of proteins associated with mitochondrial fission, enhanced lysosomal activity, and mitophagy, together with lysosomal redistribution and increased α-tubulin acetylation, suggesting improved microtubule-dependent intracellular trafficking. Quantitative proteomic analysis of four independent patient-derived HD fibroblasts corroborated these findings: GSK-3β inhibition elicited a broad set of proteins involved in cytoskeletal organization, adhesion signaling, and metabolic adaptation, whereas GSK-3α inhibition produced a more restricted and heterogeneous response. Collectively, these findings identify distinct cellular responses to selective GSK-3 isozyme inhibition and reveal GSK-3β as a predominant regulator of intracellular trafficking and mitochondrial and cytoskeletal dynamics in HD fibroblasts. Thus, inhibition of GSK-3β may represent a potential therapeutic approach for modulating HD-associated cellular dysfunction.

primary.title: Autolysosomal enhancer GHF201 attenuates pathophysiology in a mucopolysaccharidosis type I mouse model.
primary.abstract: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I (MPS-I) is a hereditary lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency in the lysosomal enzyme α-L-iduronidase (IDUA) leading to pathogenic over-accumulation of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), major constituent of connective tissue and mediators of cell signaling. We tested the therapeutic efficacy of the autolysosomal activator GHF201 in the Idua -/- mouse model of MPS-I. We show that GHF201 reduced GAGs and increased cathepsin activity in Idua -/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) and brain cells. In vivo GHF201 improved aberrant locomotion and behavior, reduced interstitial cathepsins in joints and liver, increased systemic catabolism, corrected bone dysplasia, increased autophagic flux, and ameliorated CNS neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation. GHF201 also reduced brain N-glycans, which are degraded in lysosomes. In conclusion, the lysosomal and autophagic activator GHF201 was demonstrated to improve various pathophysiological parameters in MPS-I-modeling Idua -/- female mice. Our results suggest that GHF201 can complement the inadequate Aldurazyme enzyme replacement therapy as an add-on therapy.

primary.title: A protective role for APP in nuclear waste clearance via lysosomal exocytosis.
primary.abstract: Amyloid precursor protein (APP) is widely known for its role in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis through its proteolytic processing into amyloid-β peptides. However, its physiological functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we uncover a protective role for full-length APP in facilitating the disposal of nuclear-derived debris under genotoxic stress. In both cultured cells and in vivo mouse models, loss of APP leads to nuclear waste accumulation, increased inflammation, and cell death, whereas APP overexpression mitigates these effects. Mechanistically, we show that APP supports the extracellular release of nuclear waste material through lysosomal exocytosis. APP mutants associated with familial AD fail to mediate this process. Consistently, human AD brain tissue exhibits abnormal nuclear morphology, accumulation of nuclear waste in the cytoplasm, and reduced APP levels per neuron. These findings highlight a conserved cellular mechanism by which APP contributes to nuclear and cellular homeostasis, and suggest that impaired nuclear waste clearance may represent an underappreciated contributor to neurodegeneration.

primary.title: Early reduction of myelin-associated glycoprotein at myelin membranes in Huntington's disease.
primary.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is marked by progressive neuronal loss and atrophy of grey matter structures, particularly the caudate and putamen. Brain imaging studies reveal that the white matter starts to decay in the brain of individuals bearing the HD mutation many years before symptomatic onset. However, the mechanism by which the HD mutation causes white matter loss remains to be further defined. In this study, we examined white matter pathology and explored the underlying mechanism in the HDQ140 knock-in mouse model of HD. Western blot analysis of proteins localized at different layers of the myelin sheath showed that myelin-associated glycoprotein (MAG), which is localized at the innermost myelin layer, was decreased earlier than proteins localized at outer layers of the myelin. The loss of MAG occurred at fully myelinated axons and was progressive with age. In postmortem symptomatic human HD brains, the level of MAG as well as other myelin proteins was also decreased. In HD mouse brains, MAG labeling was reduced at fiber bundles but accumulated in perinuclear structures of cells that expressed breast carcinoma amplified sequence 1, a marker for new oligodendrocytes. While their abundance was normal, new oligodendrocytes in HD brains were impeded in acquiring the expression of MAG. Compared with those in wild-type mouse brains, oligodendrocytes in HD mouse brains had a reduced frequency of MAG-bearing small vesicles and an increased abundance and enlargement of MAG-containing perinuclear structures. Further studies suggest that the MAG-accumulating perinuclear structures were derived from the late endosomal lysosomal compartment. Our study suggests that white matter decay in HD brains involves an early progressive loss of MAG in myelin membranes.

primary.title: CROP2, a Retriever-PROPPIN complex mediating protein export from endosomes to the plasma membrane in human cells.
primary.abstract: Endosomes generate tubulo-vesicular carriers to redistribute proteins between plasma membrane, Golgi, and lysosomes. These transport routes employ distinct combinations of sorting nexins with complexes such as Retromer or Retriever. We now show that, while Retromer associates with the PROPPIN WIPI1 to form the previously described CROP complex, Retriever associates with WIPI2, forming CROP2. WIPI2 integrates into Retriever-dependent coat complexes since it interacts both with the Commander subunit CCDC93 and its cognate sorting nexin SNX17. CROP and CROP2 are exclusive in their physical associations and pathway selective. Whereas CROP2 is required for endosomal exit of Integrin β1, it does not affect CROP-dependent cargos such as EGFR or GLUT1. Vice versa, CROP is not required for Integrin β1 trafficking. WIPI1 and WIPI2 rely on similar molecular features. Their activity depends on the same FSSS motif to integrate into Retromer and Retriever complexes, respectively, and on an amphipathic membrane-inserting α-helix, which conveys membrane fission activity to PROPPINs. This suggests that Retromer and Retriever coats integrate distinct PROPPIN isoforms to promote fission of the respective endosomal carriers formed by them.

secondary.title: TFEB overexpression in excitatory neurons ameliorates amyloid-β pathology via coordinated enhancement of autophagy-lysosome and mitochondrial function.
secondary.abstract: The intraneuronal accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) is an early pathogenic event in Alzheimer's disease (AD), initiating a pathological cascade that includes synaptic dysfunction, metabolic deficits, and eventual neuronal loss. Transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway (ALP) and mitochondrial homeostasis, represents a promising therapeutic target. However, its efficacy and mechanisms when specifically activated in neurons during the prodromal stage remain unclear. Here, we used an adeno-associated virus (AAV) under the control of the CaMKIIα promoter to achieve excitatory neuron-specific TFEB overexpression in the hippocampal CA1 region of 2 months-old 5×FAD mice. This intervention significantly reduced soluble Aβ levels at 3 months and attenuated amyloid plaque burden, dystrophic neurite formation, and glial activation at 6 months, accompanied by substantial improvements in spatial learning and memory. Mechanistically, transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed that TFEB not only enhanced autophagic flux and lysosomal biogenesis but also promoted the expression of key mitochondrial genes and improved mitochondrial function. In APP695swe-N2a cells, TFEB overexpression increased levels of LC3B-II and LAMP1, enhanced mitochondrial activity and biogenesis (via PGC-1α upregulation), and effectively reduced intracellular Aβ accumulation. Our findings demonstrate that targeted TFEB overexpression in excitatory neurons during early AD pathogenesis initiates a protective cascade by co-activating autophagy-lysosomal clearance and mitochondrial pathways, thereby reducing Aβ accumulation and mitigating downstream pathology. This study highlights the potential of neuron-specific TFEB activation as a cell-type-specific therapeutic approach for early AD intervention. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

secondary.title: Progranulin haploinsufficiency disrupts cathepsin D function, resulting in lysosomal abnormalities and elevated TDP-43 levels in the mouse brain.
secondary.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is a leading cause of early-onset neurodegeneration, frequently linked to mutations in the GRN gene, which encodes the protein progranulin (PGRN). PGRN is known to play a crucial role in lysosomal function, and its deficiency contributes to FTD pathogenesis. Here, we examined the consequences of PGRN loss on lysosomal homeostasis, focusing on the lysosomal protease cathepsin D (CTSD) and TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) aggregation, hallmarks of FTD and related neurodegenerative diseases. METHODS: Using mouse models with homozygous and heterozygous GRN deletions and double knockouts for GRN and CTSD, we assessed lysosomal function, CTSD expression and activity, lysosomal-associated membrane protein (LAMP) levels and localization, TDP-43 aggregation, and survival. RESULTS: PGRN deficiency resulted in significant alterations in lysosomal function. Despite significantly elevated levels of mature and immature CTSD in PGRN-deficient mice, enzymatic activity was significantly reduced. PGRN deficiency also caused accumulation of lysosomal-associated membrane protein (LAMP) and perinuclear clustering of LAMP1-positive lysosomes, suggestive of disrupted lysosomal trafficking. Correspondingly, insoluble TDP-43 levels significantly increased, implicating lysosomal impairment in defective protein degradation and aggregation. Remarkably, double-knockout mice lacking both PGRN and CTSD exhibited significantly shortened lifespans, highlighting a potential functional interaction between these proteins in maintaining neuronal health and longevity. DISCUSSION: These findings underscore the importance of PGRN as a central regulator of lysosomal function and protein homeostasis. Together, the data provide mechanistic insight into PGRN-dependent lysosomal biology and identify pathways that may contribute to GRN-associated FTD and other neurodegenerative disorders.

secondary.title: TRIM31 aggravated cerebral ischemic injury by inhibiting autophagosome-lysosome fusion through degradation of TLR9.
secondary.abstract: Recent evidence has suggested that dysfunction of the autophagy-lysosome system was a crucial factor leading to neuronal damage, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Studies have reported that Toll like receptor 9 (TLR9) is required for autophagic flux. In our investigation, we observed that TLR9 was significantly upregulated and exerted a protective role through promoting the fusion of autophagosomes and lysosomes in the stroke models. Mechanistically, we found that tripartite motif-containing protein 31 (TRIM31) interacted with TLR9 and promoted the k48-linked polyubiquitination of TLR9, consequently facilitated its degradation in a proteasome-dependent pathway. Furthermore, TRIM31 led to impaired autophagosome-lysosome fusion in cerebral ischemic injury by negatively regulating TLR9. In conclusion, we identified TRIM31 as a novel E3 ubiquitin ligase for TLR9 degradation and provided a new therapeutic strategy to alleviate ischemic brain injury by enhancing autophagosome-lysosome fusion via TLR9.

secondary.title: Enhanced Endosomal Trafficking Mediated by the Proton-Activated Chloride Channel Underlies Peripheral Sensitization in Neuropathic Pain.
secondary.abstract: Endosomal trafficking is essential for protein homeostasis, yet its role in peripheral sensitization of neuropathic pain remains unclear. Here, we identify the proton-activated chloride (PAC) channel as a critical regulator of endosomal trafficking in sensory neurons. In the spared nerve injury (SNI) model, conditional deletion of the PAC channel in sensory neurons reduced neuronal excitability, Rab5/7-dependent endocytic transport pathways, P2X3R hyperfunction, and markedly alleviated mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity. Mechanistically, SNI enhances the PAC channel function, contributing to the decreased intra-endosomal Cl- and reduced endosomal membrane tension; this promotes endosomal sorting complexes required for transport-III-dependent endosomal maturation and accelerates axonal retrograde transport of P2X3R. Last, an exploratory, locus-restricted analysis identified 2 noncoding PACC1 variants associated with the study-defined chronic-pain phenotype in a cohort study. Collectively, these findings identify PAC channel as a key regulator of intra-endosomal Cl- homeostasis and membrane tension, linking dysregulated endosomal trafficking in the nociceptor to neuropathic pain.

secondary.title: Lipid Droplet-Associated Hsp70 Palmitoylation Drives Lysosomal Dysfunction in Ischemic Stroke.
secondary.abstract: Lipid droplet (LDs) accumulate in glial cells across neurodegenerative and ischemic brain pathologies. LDs modulate cellular stress via organelle crosstalk, particularly with lysosomes, whose dysfunction and cathepsin leakage drive glial activation after cerebral ischemia. However, the molecular link between accumulated LDs and lysosomes in pathological glial activation remains incompletely understood. Using a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) model and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/Re) cell models, we found that both LD signal intensity and lysosomal cathepsin B leakage progressively increased from day 1 to day 14 after I/R. Etomoxir, an inhibitor of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1 A (CPT1A), the rate-limiting enzyme for fatty acid β-oxidation, aggravated I/R-induced LD accumulation and lysosomal damage in glial cells. Exogenous LDs derived from OGD/Re-treated glial cells aggravated lysosomal damage and promoted the proliferation of astrocytes and microglia. LD accumulation was associated with Hsp70 palmitoylation and redistribution of Hsp70 from lysosomes to the extracellular space, leading to lysosomal damage and reactive glial activation. Mechanistically, using multiple genetic and pharmacological approaches, including Plin3 knockdown, an Hsp70 palmitoylation‑site mutant, recombinant human Hsp70 (rhHsp70), as well as a pan-palmitoylation inhibitor and TLR2/4 antagonist, we consistently validated that Plin3, an LD surface protein, interacts with lysosomal Hsp70, causing Hsp70 palmitoylation and redistribution, and lysosomal damage. Extracellular Hsp70 activates TLR2/4 on glial cells, promoting cell proliferation and pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Collectively, these findings indicate that pathological LDs interacting with lysosomes drive Hsp70 palmitoylation and redistribution, causing lysosomal impairment and astrogliosis in ischemic stroke. We uncover Hsp70 palmitoylation as a potential drug target for ischemic stroke therapy.

secondary.title: A rare TMEM175 mutation drives Parkinson's disease pathology by disrupting proton gating and lysosomal acidification.
secondary.abstract: Transmembrane protein 175 (TMEM175), implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD) risk, has been variably proposed to function as a background K+ "leak" channel or a proton-activated proton channel in lysosomes. Here, we identified the rare TMEM175 variant p.L275R in a patient with early onset PD. Electrophysiological analyses revealed that TMEM175-L275R mutant proteins retain normal lysosomal expression and K+ "leak" activity, but specifically lose proton- and agonist-dependent activation gating. In skin fibroblasts isolated from the patient with PD harboring the monoallelic p.L275R mutation (TMEM175+/L275R), and in derived induced pluripotent stem cells and induced dopaminergic neurons, lysosomal H+ flux, acidification, and degradation were impaired. These lysosomal defects were corrected upon genome editing to produce the isogenic WT allele (+/+Cor), but appeared when the mutant allele was introduced onto a WT background (+/L275RMut). Pathological α-synuclein aggregation was facilitated in patient-derived (+/L275R) and mutation-introduced (+/L275RMut) neurons. Consistent with these genetic findings, pharmacological activation of TMEM175 with small-molecule agonists restored lysosomal functions and reduced α-synuclein aggregation in TMEM175+/L275R neurons. In in-vivo studies, equivalent-site-mutation knock-in mice demonstrated synucleinopathy and PD-like motor phenotypes. Collectively, our work provides genetic and pharmacological evidence that severe loss-of-function mutations may contribute causally to the onset age and pathogenesis of PD and identifies lysosomal proton channels and transporters as potential therapeutic targets for PD intervention.

secondary.title: Paclitaxel-induced disruption of lysosome motility and function in DRG neurons.
secondary.abstract: Lysosomal trafficking and homeostasis are biological functions that are pivotal for DRG neurons, given their metabolic demands and extremely long axons. Previous studies indicate that lysosomal signaling is altered in a mouse model of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) and that blocking mitogen activated protein kinase-associated kinase (MNK1/2) signaling can alleviate pain behaviors in CIPN. Here, we investigated lysosome dynamics and lysosome-associated signaling in a mouse model of CIPN induced by paclitaxel (PTX), a chemotherapeutic agent used for various types of cancer. Using spinning disk super-resolution microscope (SPINSR), we demonstrate that PTX treatment in vivo causes reduced lysosome motility observed in vitro. PTX likewise drives the accumulation of Sequestosome 1 (SQSTM1), also known as P62, in cultured mouse DRG neurons, indicating lysosomal dysfunction in DRG neurons. The transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, was also upregulated in the nucleus of cultured mouse DRG neurons treated with PTX. In line with this, increased lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1 (LAMP1) expression was observed in PTX-treated mice. Given that our previous work demonstrated PTX treatment increases MNK1/2-eIF4E signaling in DRG neurons, we examined whether MNK1/2 inhibition could rescue lysosomal dysfunction. Treatment with Tomivosertib (eFT508), a potent MNK1/2 inhibitor, restored P62 levels in DRG neurons of PTX-treated mice and reduced TFEB in DRG treated in vitro. To establish translation relevance, we further show that PTX elevates phosphorylated eiF4E (p-eIF4E) in human DRG neurons, and concurrent eFT508 administration attenuates this effect. Collectively, these findings indicated that PTX disrupts lysosome trafficking and biogenesis, and that MNK inhibition with eFT508 restores lysosomal signaling and can serve as a neuroprotective strategy for CIPN.

secondary.title: Reduced BNIP1 impairs autophagosome-lysosome fusion in hippocampal neurons and contributes to Alzheimer's disease pathology.
secondary.abstract: BNIP1 (BCL2‑interacting protein 1) belongs to the soluble N‑ethylmaleimide‑sensitive factor attachment protein receptor (SNARE) family. Statistical screening based on the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) dataset GSE48350 reveals reduced BNIP1 expression in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD), suggesting that BNIP1 is a potentially key regulatory protein for investigating AD pathogenesis. In this study, we detected BNIP1 protein levels in APP/PS1 transgenic mice and APP‑overexpressing HT22 hippocampal neuronal cells, screened key interacting proteins of BNIP1 via mass spectrometry, and further performed gain‑ and loss‑of‑function assays using overexpression plasmids and small interfering RNA (siRNA) to verify the protein function of BNIP1. Our findings indicate that, in these experimental models, reduced BNIP1 expression contributes to AD‑related pathological alterations by impairing autophagosome‑lysosome fusion. Restoration of BNIP1 expression enhances Rab5b‑mediated Rab7 recruitment and consequently ameliorates autophagosome‑lysosome fusion. secondary.title: Endosomal signalling of protease-activated receptor-2 amplifies histamine-induced pain of irritable bowel syndrome.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND.: Proteases and histamine, co-secreted by mast cells and bacteria, sensitize colonic nociceptors and contribute to irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) pain. OBJECTIVE.: To determine whether irreversible proteolytic cleavage of protease-activated receptor-2 (PAR2) and its continued activity in endosomes amplify and sustain otherwise transient pronociceptive actions of histamine receptors (HRs) to cause recurrent pain, the defining symptom of IBS. DESIGN.: We investigated PAR2 and H1R coexpression in nociceptors using RNAscope and assessed the consequences of coactivation using electrophysiological assays of nociceptor sensitization and biophysical measurements of receptor and effector activity. RESULTS.: PAR2 and H1R were coexpressed by human and mouse dorsal root ganglion nociceptors. Intracolonic infusion of fecal supernatants from IBS patients with elevated histamine and proteolytic activity enhanced mechanosensitivity of colonic nociceptors in mice. Antagonists of PAR2 or H1R abolished this response. Combined administration of subthreshold concentrations of trypsin and histamine replicated the effects of fecal supernatant and caused hyperexcitability of isolated nociceptors. Pre-activation with trypsin sensitized histamine-induced hyperexcitability in nociceptors from wild-type but not Par2−/− mice. Endocytosis inhibitors prevented this hypersensitivity, consistent with sustained endosomal signaling of PAR2 and persistent nociceptor hyperexcitability. Trypsin amplified histamine-induced activation of H1R and β-arrestin2 and Gαq effectors at the plasmalemma and in endosomes. Conversely, histamine did not sensitize trypsin-induced hyperexcitability of neurons, in line with the inability of histamine to induce sustained nociceptor hypersensitivity. CONCLUSIONS.: By amplifying and maintaining the otherwise transient actions of H1R and possibly other pain receptors, persistent PAR2 endosomal signaling makes a dominant contribution to IBS-related colonic pain.

secondary.title: Aβ-induced CaMKII hyperactivation is associated with impaired lysosomal maturation and mitophagy.
secondary.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ)-associated synaptic failure, intracellular Ca2+ dysregulation, and progressive impairment of lysosome-dependent clearance pathways. Aβ induces sustained Ca2+ overload, resulting in pathological hyperactivation of CaMKII, which normally participates in the regulation of autophagy. However, whether CaMKII hyperactivation contributes to Aβ-induced late-stage autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction and mitophagy failure remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the effects of the CaMKII inhibitor KN93 in Aβ25-35-exposed rat organotypic hippocampal slice cultures (OHSCs, ex vivo model) and the mouse brain in vivo. The results showed that Aβ25-35 induced intracellular Ca2+ elevation, CaMKII hyperactivation, and marked accumulation of LC3-II and p62. Ultrastructural and biochemical analyses revealed impaired lysosomal maturation, defective autophagosome-lysosome coupling, and accumulation of autophagic vacuoles, consistent with a blockade of late-stage autophagic flux. Increased levels of immature cathepsin D and reduced colocalization of LC3 with lysosomal markers further supported compromised lysosomal competence. Damaged mitochondria were recruited to lysosomal compartments but failed to undergo effective degradation, indicating abortive mitophagy under Aβ25-35 exposure. KN93 attenuated Aβ25-35-induced defects in lysosomal protease maturation, autophagosome-lysosome fusion, and mitochondrial clearance in both the ex vivo OHSCs model and the in vivo mouse brain. KN93 also ameliorated cognitive impairment in Aβ25-35-exposed mice. Taken together, these findings indicate that CaMKII hyperactivation contributes to Aβ25-35-induced autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction and neuronal damage, and that pharmacological inhibition of CaMKII with KN93 restores intracellular degradative capacity and ameliorates cognitive impairment under Aβ stress.

secondary.title: Lysosome-targeted near-infrared fluorescent probe ROCL enables dynamic hypochlorous acid imaging in living cells and a mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
secondary.abstract: Hypochlorous acid (HClO) plays critical roles in oxidative stress and is strongly implicated in the progression of Parkinson's disease (PD). Here, we report ROCL, a new lysosome-targeted near-infrared fluorescent probe for sensitive and selective detection of HClO in living systems. ROCL displays rapid response, excellent selectivity, and a low detection limit of 49 nM, based on an HClO-induced spirolactam ring-opening mechanism. The probe enables real-time imaging of exogenous and endogenous HClO in SH-SY5Y and PC12 cells, exhibits low cytotoxicity, and effectively visualizes elevated HClO levels in MPTP- and rotenone-induced PD models. ROCL also shows favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and allows noninvasive in vivo HClO imaging in PD model mice. These results establish ROCL as a valuable tool for probing HClO-associated oxidative stress in neurodegenerative diseases.

secondary.title: Nano Proton Scavengers Modulate Endosomal pH to Inhibit Microglial Activation and Enhance Stroke Recovery.
secondary.abstract: Endosomes play a crucial role in immune regulation, yet their effect on microglial behavior in ischemic stroke is not well-documented. While drug-loaded nanoparticles can modulate microglial inflammation, their intrinsic biological effects on microglial activation are underexplored. We demonstrate that inhibiting endosomal acidification reduces pro-inflammatory microglial polarization, limits pathological engulfment of neurons, and reduces neuronal apoptosis. To achieve the same effects in vivo, building on a validated dual-site buffering mechanism of sulfonated chitosan, we develop sulfonated Nano Proton Scavengers (sNPS) as a materials-based strategy to modulate endo/lysosomal pH. After cerebral ischemia, sNPS showed greater fluorescence-associated enrichment in the ipsilateral than in the contralateral hemisphere and was associated with brain-resident and infiltrating immune-cell populations. In the injured brain, sNPS alleviated endo/lysosomal acid stress, suppressed TLR3/4-linked inflammatory signaling, and normalized inflammation-driven endo/lysosomal remodeling and proton-loading machinery, thereby restraining maladaptive microglial activation. This immunomodulation was accompanied by improved neural structural preservation and post-stroke survival and functional outcomes. These findings identify endosomal pH homeostasis as a tractable intracellular cue for material-driven immunoregulation and suggest that sNPS offers a complementary therapeutic direction for ischemic stroke.

best.title: ALS-linked FUS mutation impairs GEMIN5-dependent mRNA recruitment to neuronal late endosomes.
best.abstract: Neurons depend on tightly regulated positioning of cellular components to maintain long-distance signaling, but the mechanisms guiding specific mRNAs to distant regions remain unclear. Here, we show that late endosomes function as selective RNA carriers in human motor neurons and uncover the molecular logic guiding their loading. Using APEX2-mediated proximity labeling, we identify the external transcriptome of RAB7A-positive endosomes and find a specific population of mRNAs enriched for endosomal, axonal, and synaptic functions. We find that mRNAs enriched in RAB7A endosomes contain evolutionarily conserved 5'UTRs that act as localization signals, and that the RNA-binding protein GEMIN5 interacts with these regions to promote endosomal RNA recruitment. Finally, we show that there is a conspicuous loss of endosome-associated transcripts in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-associated conditions, accompanied by the mislocalization of GEMIN5 from endosomes. These findings uncover fundamental principles of RNA compartmentalization and highlight endosomal mRNA loading as a vulnerable axis in neuronal homeostasis.
