secondary.title: An Optimized Stem Cell Secretome Proteomics Platform: Application to Progranulin-Deficient iPSCs.
secondary.abstract: Stem cells secrete diverse extracellular proteins that regulate pluripotency, differentiation, and cell-cell communication, making them powerful model systems for studying development, disease mechanisms, and regenerative medicine. However, robust stem cell secretome analysis remains technically challenging. Unlike many other cell types, pluripotent stem cells cannot tolerate serum starvation or growth factor deprivation, while low-abundance secreted proteins are often masked by media-derived proteins and intracellular contamination. Here, we systematically optimized the secretome proteomics workflow in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) by evaluating culture medium composition, conditioned-media collection time, cell plating density, media harvest and preparation methods, LC-MS acquisition methods, and data analysis strategies. Full-strength Essential 8 medium, 48 h media collection, 80% cell confluency, two-step centrifugation, and data-independent acquisition (DIA)LC-MS/MS provided the optimal secretome proteomics data quality. We then applied the optimized platform to an isogenic iPSC disease model to investigate how progranulin deficiency reshapes the extracellular and intracellular proteomes. Progranulin-deficient iPSCs showed a coordinated reduction of extracellular lysosomal hydrolases despite relatively modest intracellular proteome changes, suggesting altered lysosome trafficking and possible impairment of lysosomal exocytosis. Together, this work establishes a robust and standardized workflow for stem cell secretome proteomics and demonstrates its utility for investigating extracellular proteome remodeling in human disease models.

secondary.title: A minimally invasive protocol for cerebrospinal fluid collection in mice and small-volume proteomics.
secondary.abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is a valuable resource for pre-clinical drug discovery, as it can be used to detect biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases and overall brain health and function. Here, we describe a protocol for collecting CSF from mice. This minimally invasive approach enables serial collections and longitudinal analysis of CSF samples from the same mouse. We also describe steps for quality control and proteomic analysis.

secondary.title: Metabolomics Profiling of Serum Small Extracellular Vesicle-Enriched Fractions Across Early Post-Injury Intervals Following Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
secondary.abstract: Severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) induces metabolic disturbances that remain difficult to assess non-invasively. This exploratory study compared metabolomics profiles of serum small extracellular vesicle-enriched fractions from healthy controls and patients with sTBI sampled at days 1, 3, and 5 post-injury. Using high-resolution liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), we identified metabolite differences associated with each sampled post-injury interval. Principal component analysis showed group-level separation between controls and the individual post-injury interval groups, with the largest separation observed in the day 1 comparison. N-Acetyl-l-aspartic acid, a canonical marker of neuronal integrity, showed lower abundance in the day 1 group relative to controls, whereas PGF2α ethanolamide showed lower abundance relative to controls in all three interval-specific comparisons. Glu-ser and tryptophan also met the differential-abundance criteria in more than one interval vs. control comparison. Ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) linked the day 1 metabolite alterations to literature-curated neurological functions, including demyelination and neurodegeneration; however, these associations are presented as hypothesis-generating. Collectively, these findings identify serum small extracellular vesicle-enriched fraction metabolite alterations associated with sTBI for further investigation in fully longitudinal sTBI cohorts.

secondary.title: A comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas of hippocampal microglia in a mouse model of traumatic brain injury.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers microglial activation and disrupts the inflammatory microenvironment in the hippocampus, which are key contributors to neuroinflammation and subsequent secondary brain damage. Nevertheless, the cellular heterogeneity of microglia, their pro-inflammatory activation mechanisms, and microenvironmental regulatory networks have not been fully characterized. METHODS: By integrating multi-source single-cell transcriptomic datasets and establishing a mouse TBI validation model, we constructed a high-resolution cellular atlas of hippocampal microglia. Through comprehensive re-analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets, bioinformatic approaches, high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), cell-cell communication profiling, and in vivo behavioral and in vivo pathological evaluations, we thoroughly explored the subpopulation diversity, functional features, and regulatory mechanisms of hippocampal microglia following TBI. RESULTS: TBI elicited extensive phenotypic diversification in hippocampal microglia, and five major subpopulations were identified, among which disease-associated microglia (DAM) were further classified into four distinct subclusters. A distinct inflamed DAM subset (Inflam-DAM) was found to highly express canonical pro-inflammatory signature genes. Transcriptomic profiling revealed enrichment of AP-1 family transcription factors and the IL-17 signaling pathway in this subset, confirming its robust pro-inflammatory phenotype. hdWGCNA demonstrated that the pro-inflammatory state of Inflam-DAM was tightly linked to transcriptional and translational regulation. Cell-cell communication analysis indicated that meningeal macrophages, B cells and fibroblasts acted as upstream regulators and selectively interacted with DAM subclusters in the inflammatory niche. In turn, activated DAM communicated with neurons in an injury-dependent manner, eventually impairing neurogenesis. In vivo experiments validated that TBI mice displayed severe neurological dysfunction, elevated expression of pro-inflammatory microglial markers and signaling molecules in the hippocampus, and fewer newborn mature neurons - all findings consistent with our single-cell data. CONCLUSION: In summary, this work constructs a full-scale single-cell transcriptomic landscape of hippocampal microglia in TBI mice. We systematically delineated the heterogeneity of DAM subsets, the pro-inflammatory regulatory mechanism of Inflam-DAM, and the multi-layered intercellular network within the inflammatory microenvironment. Our results deepen the mechanistic understanding of TBI-associated neuroinflammation and offer valuable clues for the development of targeted anti-inflammatory therapies.

secondary.title: Impaired cellular stress adaptability in Alzheimer's disease patient-derived fibroblasts: a PFKFB3-linked transcriptomic response to oxidative stress.
secondary.abstract: Aging-related impairment in cellular stress adaptability may contribute to vulnerability to Alzheimer's disease (AD), but patient-derived experimental models that preserve agingassociated molecular features remain underused. Here, we investigated transcriptomic responses to oxidative stress in ex vivo dermal fibroblasts derived from patients with AD and control participants matched for age and sex. Fibroblasts were exposed to hydrogen peroxide to induce reactive oxygen species-mediated stress, followed by RNA sequencing to identify disease-associated differences in stress-responsive gene regulation. AD-derived fibroblasts exhibited distinct oxidative stress response patterns, with altered regulation of pathways related to endoplasmic reticulum stress, immune activation, autophagy, protein synthesis, and cell cycle control. Systematic candidate gene prioritization identified PFKFB3 as a key stress-responsive gene showing reduced induction in AD fibroblasts. Lower PFKFB3 responsiveness was associated with poorer cognitive performance and higher levels of neurodegeneration-related blood biomarkers, including plasma pTau217, neurofilament light chain, and glial fibrillary acidic protein. In immortalized human astrocytes, PFKFB3 knockdown reduced cell viability under oxidative stress and altered transcriptional programs related to proteostasis, metabolic regulation, and immune activation. These findings suggest that AD is associated with impaired cellular stress adaptability in patient-derived fibroblasts and highlight PFKFB3 as a candidate node linking oxidative stress responsiveness, glial vulnerability, and AD-related pathological burden.

secondary.title: PRKN-independent mitophagy regulators in dopaminergic neurons identified by genome-wide CRISPR screening.
secondary.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. Genetic and epidemiological studies have suggested that mitochondrial dysfunction is implicated in the development of PD. PRKN/Parkin is known to play an essential role in mitochondrial quality control and mitophagy. Indeed, mutations and inactivation of this gene are associated with hereditary and idiopathic forms of PD. Despite extensive studies on PRKN-dependent mitophagy, the molecular regulators of PRKN-independent mitophagy in dopaminergic neurons remain incompletely understood. We generated a PRKN knockout iPSC-derived dopaminergic neuronal line expressing the fluorescent mitophagy biosensor mito-SRAI, which reports the delivery of mitochondria to lysosomes as an increase in the TOLLES/YPet fluorescence ratio. We used this cell line to conduct a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen to reveal genetic regulators involved in PRKN-independent mitophagy. Dozens of genes were identified whose knockout increased the TOLLES/YPet ratio in an uncoupler-dependent manner. Of these, several genes emerged as candidates with potential therapeutic implications, one of which was Cathepsin F (CTSF). CCCP treatment increased the TOLLES/YPet ratio in neurons with siRNA-mediated CTSF knockdown, and CTSF knockdown partially preserved the proportion of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive dopaminergic neurons after paraquat exposure. These results suggest that CTSF is a candidate regulator of PRKN-independent mitophagy and that this lysosomal enzyme may represent a potentially druggable candidate target for PD.

secondary.title: Machine learning-assisted plasma PEA proteomics enables differential diagnosis of melancholic depression and bipolar disorder.
secondary.abstract: Differentiating bipolar disorder (BD) from major depressive disorder (MDD) remains a critical unmet need in psychiatry due to overlapping clinical presentations and the absence of reliable biological markers. In this study, we assessed the capacity of multivariate machine learning models to accurately differentiate BD from MDD with melancholic features using plasma proteomic profiles obtained via Proximity Extension Assay (PEA) technology. A total of 67 participants were included (23 BD, 20 MDD, and 24 HC), and plasma protein expression was assessed using the Olink Target 96 Neurology panel. Differential proteomic analysis revealed distinct disorder-specific expression patterns, identifying 21 differentially expressed proteins in BD versus MDD, 18 in BD versus healthy controls, and 7 in MDD versus healthy controls. Using a stepwise feature reduction strategy, machine learning models were trained on three feature sets comprising all proteins, the top 20 most informative proteins, and the top 5 most beneficial proteins, and evaluated across BD-MDD, BD-HC, and MDD-HC classification tasks using five algorithms. For BD-MDD discrimination, the Random Forest model achieved the highest performance when trained on the top 5 protein set (LXN, HAGH, MATN3, PLXNB1, and CTSC), yielding an AUC of 0.905, with similarly strong performance observed using the top 20 protein set. Feature importance analysis highlighted proteins involved in neurodevelopmental processes, immune regulation, and extracellular matrix organization. Overall, these findings demonstrate that integrating plasma proteomics with machine learning enables robust differentiation between BD and MDD with melancholic features, supporting the development of scalable and biologically informed diagnostic tools for precision psychiatry.

best.title: Functional transcriptomic profile of mouse controlled cortical impact model of post-traumatic epilepsy with robust spontaneous recurrent seizures.
best.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of acquired epilepsy, yet the molecular changes linking the initial injury to post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) remain incompletely understood. Here, we used a severe controlled cortical impact mouse model that develops robust spontaneous recurrent seizures to characterize the temporal and regional progression of post-traumatic transcriptional responses. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on the contralateral cortex and hippocampus collected from TBI and time-matched sham mice at 7, 21, and 60 days after injury, corresponding to the acute injury, latent period, and chronic epilepsy phases, respectively. Transcriptomic changes were characterized using differentially expressed gene (DEG) analysis, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes gene-set enrichment analyses, and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Transcriptomic responses were strongly dependent on brain region and disease phase. At 7 days, the cortex showed enhanced neuronal and structural signaling alongside suppression of immune, metabolic, and cell-cycle processes, whereas the hippocampus showed prominent neuroimmune activation and metabolic stress. By 21 days, before the emergence of spontaneous seizures, the hippocampus shifted toward partial normalization of metabolic pathway enrichment, accompanied by suppression of neurotransmission, synaptic plasticity, and neuronal organization. In contrast, the cortex showed increased enrichment of immune and tissue-remodeling processes. Although relatively few DEGs were detected at 60 days, a selective hippocampal signature persisted after PTE was established. Pathway analyses converged on coordinated changes in neuroimmune, metabolic, lipid-regulatory, and synaptic processes. Upstream Regulator Analysis further identified a temporal reversal in APOE-associated regulatory activity, linking inflammatory and lipid-metabolic responses with later synaptic remodeling. The 21-day post-injury hippocampus represents a critical disease-modification window. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that PTE progression involves phase-specific molecular remodeling that shifts from an early cortical response to sustained hippocampal dysregulation. The latent hippocampal signature identifies a potentially actionable molecular window before recurrent seizure onset.

best.title: Integrated serum metabolomics and hippocampal transcriptomics reveal metabolic reprogramming associated with BBB impairment and hippocampal injury in HFD-fed mice.
best.abstract: AIMS: Increasing evidence suggests that high-fat diet (HFD) consumption induces systemic metabolic disturbances and is associated with blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction and hippocampal injury. This study aimed to explore the potential mechanisms linking HFD-induced metabolic disturbances to BBB and hippocampal abnormalities. METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed an HFD or a normal diet (ND) for 12 weeks. Systemic metabolic and inflammatory status, hepatic lipid accumulation, neurobehavioral performance, hippocampal injury, BBB integrity, and hippocampal inflammatory alterations were systematically assessed. Integrated serum untargeted metabolomics and hippocampal transcriptomics were performed to identify key molecular pathways. RESULTS: HFD-fed mice exhibited systemic metabolic disturbances, increased BBB permeability, hippocampal neuronal injury and inflammation, and impaired motor coordination. Integrated serum metabolomic and hippocampal transcriptomic analyses identified alterations in histidine and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Hippocampal transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulation of carnosine dipeptidase 1 (Cndp1) and phospholipase A2 group IVE (Pla2g4e) and downregulation of diacylglycerol kinase kappa (Dgkk) and ethanolamine-phosphate phospho-lyase (Etnppl), which were further validated by RT-qPCR. Serum metabolomic analysis further revealed decreased serum carnosine levels. Given the reported neuroprotective properties of carnosine, we further investigated its effects in palmitic acid-treated HT22 cells. Carnosine improved cell viability, attenuated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and modulated the expression of Cndp1, Pla2g4e, Etnppl, and Dgkk. CONCLUSION: HFD was associated with BBB impairment, hippocampal inflammatory activation, neuronal injury, and behavioral alterations. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses implicated histidine and glycerophospholipid metabolism associated with HFD-induced metabolic disturbances and hippocampal injury.

best.title: Proteomic Analysis of Plasma Small Extracellular Vesicles and Targeted Metabolomic Analysis of Plasma From Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
best.abstract: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder with deficits in social communication and interaction, restricted and repetitive behaviors, and unusual stereotyped interests or activities. With a lack of molecular information on the etiology of ASD, early diagnosis of this disease remains a challenge. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), as extracellular vesicles containing various important biomolecules, have been demonstrated to have a functional impact on physiological processes in the central nervous system. Herein, we profiled the proteome of plasma sEVs collected from preschool children with autism and performed targeted metabolic analysis on their plasma samples. Screening of the differentiated proteins between autistic and healthy children revealed potential biomarkers, including those involved in calcium ion binding, such as MACF1 and CALM3. Bioinformatic investigation further identified 10 outlier proteins, such as EHD1 and ERF3A, strongly associated with autism. Targeted metabolic analysis and IPA prediction suggested the potential involvement of the PI3K-AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. The sEV proteomic and plasma metabolomic analyses were performed in parallel, and pathway-level findings from each dataset were compared descriptively. These results provide insight into the biological mechanism of autism and promise in determining biomarkers for the early diagnosis of ASD. best.title: A unified framework for scalable differential testing for spatial omics.
best.abstract: A key challenge in spatial omics is identifying features whose values vary depending on both cell type and the surrounding cellular niche. Existing methods designed for spatial transcriptomic data do not generalize well to modalities beyond count-based data and do not scale efficiently to current data volumes. Here we introduce spotGLM, a mixture-aware generalized linear modeling framework for cell-type-specific differential testing across spatial modalities, and SPARROW, a power-preserving data distillation strategy for scalable inference. SpotGLM accommodates diverse data types including count-based gene expression, binomial isoform proportions and continuous chromatin accessibility scores within a unified statistical framework. We demonstrate the framework across spatial omics applications. On Visium HD data of colorectal cancer and mouse kidney, we recover cell-type-specific niche effects with serial-slice cross-platform validation. On long-read spatial RNA-seq data, we resolve cell-type-specific isoform switching in the mouse olfactory bulb. On spatial ATAC-seq data from mouse brain, we recover cell-type-specific spatial variation in regulatory motif accessibility.

best.title: Parkinson's disease-linked D620N mutation selectively alters the brain-specific protein interactome of VPS35.
best.abstract: Mutations in several genes are known to cause familial forms of Parkinson's disease (PD), including mutations in the vacuolar protein sorting 35 ortholog (VPS35) gene linked to late-onset, autosomal dominant PD. VPS35 encodes a core subunit of the retromer complex which functions in endosomal sorting and recycling. It remains unclear how the pathogenic D620N mutation in VPS35 disrupts retromer function to induce neurodegeneration in PD. Using cell- and rodent-based models expressing D620N VPS35, we performed interactome proteomics to identify alterations underlying the pathogenic effects of D620N VPS35 in PD. Using overexpression of VPS35 variants in HEK-293 T cells, we conducted tandem affinity purification (TAP) or co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) with protein chemical crosslinking to determine the native and non-native protein interactomes of wild-type (WT) and D620N VPS35, respectively. Notably, we can confirm the reduced interaction of D620N VPS35 with components of the WASH complex. Additionally, using a viral-mediated gene transfer model of human D620N VPS35 overexpression in adult rat brain, we identify the first brain-specific protein interactome of VPS35. These overexpression models reveal remarkably similar interaction profiles of WT and D620N VPS35, suggesting that the D620N mutation has a subtle effect on the overall VPS35 protein interactome. We also conducted proteomic analysis of brain tissue from a D620N VPS35 knockin (KI) mouse model that expresses VPS35 at endogenous levels. Using co-IP from hemibrain or striatal extracts of WT and D620N VPS35 KI mice, we reveal a high degree of similarity between the brain interactomes of WT and D620N VPS35, further suggesting a subtle effect of the D620N mutation on VPS35 protein interactions. Notably, in both hemibrain and striatum, we find a selective decrease in the interaction of two known interactors, TBC1D5 and VPS29, with D620N VPS35. We also performed global proteomic analysis of striatal tissue from D620N VPS35 KI mice and reveal a high degree of similarity between WT and D620N, further suggesting a subtle effect of this mutation. Together, our study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the VPS35 protein interactome and reveals a selective effect of the PD-linked D620N mutation in mammalian cells and brain. Our study provides key insight into the mechanisms of retromer dysfunction in VPS35-linked PD.

best.title: Cellular morphology emerges from polygenic, distributed transcriptional variation.
best.abstract: Height and disease risk are canonical polygenic traits, but whether an analogous architecture governs cellular phenotypes remains unclear. Here, we show that cellular morphology behaves as a polygenic systems phenotype by integrating cross-modal modeling, perturbation profiling, and human genetic variation. An adversarially aligned autoencoder trained on four perturbation datasets predicted morphology from gene expression and generalized without retraining to matched RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and cell painting profiles from 100 genetically diverse induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) donors. Seventeen morphological features were strongly predicted, particularly those capturing organelle distribution and cytoskeletal architecture. Predictive signal was broadly distributed across genes, with weak individual gene-morphology correlations. Independent CRISPR perturbations supported model-prioritized genes including TIAM1, RAB31, and ABCC5, while genetic analyses identified variant-gene-morphology associations involving PDHX, SLC11A2, and MAPKAPK5. These findings extend polygenic models of complex traits to cellular architecture and provide a framework for interpreting cross-modal prediction in functional genomics.

best.title: An Optimized Stem Cell Secretome Proteomics Platform: Application to Progranulin-Deficient iPSCs.
best.abstract: Stem cells secrete diverse extracellular proteins that regulate pluripotency, differentiation, and cell-cell communication, making them powerful model systems for studying development, disease mechanisms, and regenerative medicine. However, robust stem cell secretome analysis remains technically challenging. Unlike many other cell types, pluripotent stem cells cannot tolerate serum starvation or growth factor deprivation, while low-abundance secreted proteins are often masked by media-derived proteins and intracellular contamination. Here, we systematically optimized the secretome proteomics workflow in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) by evaluating culture medium composition, conditioned-media collection time, cell plating density, media harvest and preparation methods, LC-MS acquisition methods, and data analysis strategies. Full-strength Essential 8 medium, 48 h media collection, 80% cell confluency, two-step centrifugation, and data-independent acquisition (DIA)LC-MS/MS provided the optimal secretome proteomics data quality. We then applied the optimized platform to an isogenic iPSC disease model to investigate how progranulin deficiency reshapes the extracellular and intracellular proteomes. Progranulin-deficient iPSCs showed a coordinated reduction of extracellular lysosomal hydrolases despite relatively modest intracellular proteome changes, suggesting altered lysosome trafficking and possible impairment of lysosomal exocytosis. Together, this work establishes a robust and standardized workflow for stem cell secretome proteomics and demonstrates its utility for investigating extracellular proteome remodeling in human disease models.

best.title: Metabolomics Profiling of Serum Small Extracellular Vesicle-Enriched Fractions Across Early Post-Injury Intervals Following Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
best.abstract: Severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) induces metabolic disturbances that remain difficult to assess non-invasively. This exploratory study compared metabolomics profiles of serum small extracellular vesicle-enriched fractions from healthy controls and patients with sTBI sampled at days 1, 3, and 5 post-injury. Using high-resolution liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), we identified metabolite differences associated with each sampled post-injury interval. Principal component analysis showed group-level separation between controls and the individual post-injury interval groups, with the largest separation observed in the day 1 comparison. N-Acetyl-l-aspartic acid, a canonical marker of neuronal integrity, showed lower abundance in the day 1 group relative to controls, whereas PGF2α ethanolamide showed lower abundance relative to controls in all three interval-specific comparisons. Glu-ser and tryptophan also met the differential-abundance criteria in more than one interval vs. control comparison. Ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) linked the day 1 metabolite alterations to literature-curated neurological functions, including demyelination and neurodegeneration; however, these associations are presented as hypothesis-generating. Collectively, these findings identify serum small extracellular vesicle-enriched fraction metabolite alterations associated with sTBI for further investigation in fully longitudinal sTBI cohorts.

best.title: A comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas of hippocampal microglia in a mouse model of traumatic brain injury.
best.abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers microglial activation and disrupts the inflammatory microenvironment in the hippocampus, which are key contributors to neuroinflammation and subsequent secondary brain damage. Nevertheless, the cellular heterogeneity of microglia, their pro-inflammatory activation mechanisms, and microenvironmental regulatory networks have not been fully characterized. METHODS: By integrating multi-source single-cell transcriptomic datasets and establishing a mouse TBI validation model, we constructed a high-resolution cellular atlas of hippocampal microglia. Through comprehensive re-analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets, bioinformatic approaches, high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), cell-cell communication profiling, and in vivo behavioral and in vivo pathological evaluations, we thoroughly explored the subpopulation diversity, functional features, and regulatory mechanisms of hippocampal microglia following TBI. RESULTS: TBI elicited extensive phenotypic diversification in hippocampal microglia, and five major subpopulations were identified, among which disease-associated microglia (DAM) were further classified into four distinct subclusters. A distinct inflamed DAM subset (Inflam-DAM) was found to highly express canonical pro-inflammatory signature genes. Transcriptomic profiling revealed enrichment of AP-1 family transcription factors and the IL-17 signaling pathway in this subset, confirming its robust pro-inflammatory phenotype. hdWGCNA demonstrated that the pro-inflammatory state of Inflam-DAM was tightly linked to transcriptional and translational regulation. Cell-cell communication analysis indicated that meningeal macrophages, B cells and fibroblasts acted as upstream regulators and selectively interacted with DAM subclusters in the inflammatory niche. In turn, activated DAM communicated with neurons in an injury-dependent manner, eventually impairing neurogenesis. In vivo experiments validated that TBI mice displayed severe neurological dysfunction, elevated expression of pro-inflammatory microglial markers and signaling molecules in the hippocampus, and fewer newborn mature neurons - all findings consistent with our single-cell data. CONCLUSION: In summary, this work constructs a full-scale single-cell transcriptomic landscape of hippocampal microglia in TBI mice. We systematically delineated the heterogeneity of DAM subsets, the pro-inflammatory regulatory mechanism of Inflam-DAM, and the multi-layered intercellular network within the inflammatory microenvironment. Our results deepen the mechanistic understanding of TBI-associated neuroinflammation and offer valuable clues for the development of targeted anti-inflammatory therapies.

best.title: Impaired cellular stress adaptability in Alzheimer's disease patient-derived fibroblasts: a PFKFB3-linked transcriptomic response to oxidative stress.
best.abstract: Aging-related impairment in cellular stress adaptability may contribute to vulnerability to Alzheimer's disease (AD), but patient-derived experimental models that preserve agingassociated molecular features remain underused. Here, we investigated transcriptomic responses to oxidative stress in ex vivo dermal fibroblasts derived from patients with AD and control participants matched for age and sex. Fibroblasts were exposed to hydrogen peroxide to induce reactive oxygen species-mediated stress, followed by RNA sequencing to identify disease-associated differences in stress-responsive gene regulation. AD-derived fibroblasts exhibited distinct oxidative stress response patterns, with altered regulation of pathways related to endoplasmic reticulum stress, immune activation, autophagy, protein synthesis, and cell cycle control. Systematic candidate gene prioritization identified PFKFB3 as a key stress-responsive gene showing reduced induction in AD fibroblasts. Lower PFKFB3 responsiveness was associated with poorer cognitive performance and higher levels of neurodegeneration-related blood biomarkers, including plasma pTau217, neurofilament light chain, and glial fibrillary acidic protein. In immortalized human astrocytes, PFKFB3 knockdown reduced cell viability under oxidative stress and altered transcriptional programs related to proteostasis, metabolic regulation, and immune activation. These findings suggest that AD is associated with impaired cellular stress adaptability in patient-derived fibroblasts and highlight PFKFB3 as a candidate node linking oxidative stress responsiveness, glial vulnerability, and AD-related pathological burden.

We generated a PRKN knockout iPSC-derived dopaminergic neuronal line expressing the fluorescent mitophagy biosensor mito-SRAI, which reports the delivery of mitochondria to lysosomes as an increase in the TOLLES/YPet fluorescence ratio. We used this cell line to conduct a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen to reveal genetic regulators involved in PRKN-independent mitophagy. Dozens of genes were identified whose knockout increased the TOLLES/YPet ratio in an uncoupler-dependent manner. Of these, several genes emerged as candidates with potential therapeutic implications, one of which was Cathepsin F (CTSF). CCCP treatment increased the TOLLES/YPet ratio in neurons with siRNA-mediated CTSF knockdown, and CTSF knockdown partially preserved the proportion of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive dopaminergic neurons after paraquat exposure. These results suggest that CTSF is a candidate regulator of PRKN-independent mitophagy and that this lysosomal enzyme may represent a potentially druggable candidate target for PD.

best.title: Machine learning-assisted plasma PEA proteomics enables differential diagnosis of melancholic depression and bipolar disorder.
best.abstract: Differentiating bipolar disorder (BD) from major depressive disorder (MDD) remains a critical unmet need in psychiatry due to overlapping clinical presentations and the absence of reliable biological markers. In this study, we assessed the capacity of multivariate machine learning models to accurately differentiate BD from MDD with melancholic features using plasma proteomic profiles obtained via Proximity Extension Assay (PEA) technology. A total of 67 participants were included (23 BD, 20 MDD, and 24 HC), and plasma protein expression was assessed using the Olink Target 96 Neurology panel. Differential proteomic analysis revealed distinct disorder-specific expression patterns, identifying 21 differentially expressed proteins in BD versus MDD, 18 in BD versus healthy controls, and 7 in MDD versus healthy controls. Using a stepwise feature reduction strategy, machine learning models were trained on three feature sets comprising all proteins, the top 20 most informative proteins, and the top 5 most beneficial proteins, and evaluated across BD-MDD, BD-HC, and MDD-HC classification tasks using five algorithms. For BD-MDD discrimination, the Random Forest model achieved the highest performance when trained on the top 5 protein set (LXN, HAGH, MATN3, PLXNB1, and CTSC), yielding an AUC of 0.905, with similarly strong performance observed using the top 20 protein set. Feature importance analysis highlighted proteins involved in neurodevelopmental processes, immune regulation, and extracellular matrix organization. Overall, these findings demonstrate that integrating plasma proteomics with machine learning enables robust differentiation between BD and MDD with melancholic features, supporting the development of scalable and biologically informed diagnostic tools for precision psychiatry.

primary.title: Ribosome-associated vesicles promote activity-dependent local translation in neurons.
primary.abstract: Local protein synthesis in axons and dendrites underpins synaptic plasticity. However, the composition of the protein synthesis machinery in distal neuronal processes and the mechanisms for its deployment to local translation sites remain unclear. Here, we employed multi-scale imaging that combines cryo-electron tomography, volume electron microscopy, and live-cell imaging to identify endoplasmic reticulum-derived KDEL-positive vesicles, a subset of which are decorated with ribosomes (Ribosome-Associated Vesicles, RAVs) in neurites. We demonstrate that neuronal stimulation triggers compartment-specific responses: dendrites accumulate stationary KDEL-positive vesicles at sites of enhanced translation, while axons accelerate vesicle transport. cLTP stimulation additionally increases the proportion of KDEL-positive vesicles that carry ribosomes, expanding the local RAV pool. Real-time imaging of translation at single mRNA resolution reveals that RAV-associated translation sites exhibit ∼30% greater nascent-peptide signal amplitude compared to periods without RAV association, indicating that RAVs boost local translation output. These findings establish RAVs as specialized platforms that integrate activity-dependent signals with local protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how neurons achieve precise spatiotemporal control of translation.

primary.title: Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy.
primary.abstract: High-numerical-aperture (NA) oblique plane microscopy enables noninvasive fluorescence imaging of subcellular dynamics without radical sample modification. However, performance degrades at depth in multicellular specimens as scattering and refractive-index heterogeneity raise out-of-focus background. We report a two-photon oblique plane microscope that improves resolution at depth by combining high-NA single-objective detection with multiphoton plane illumination. The microscope achieves ~ 300 nm lateral and ~ 650 nm axial resolution, with single-molecule sensitivity and < 60 nm localization precision in vivo. Compared with two-photon point scanning, the lower illumination NA delivers order-of-magnitude lower peak intensity, enabling > 5 × faster volumetric acquisition (up to 3.25 × 106 voxels s-1). In multicellular contexts, near-infrared nonlinear excitation enhances contrast throughout the illumination depth by ~ 2 × and restores volumetric resolving power by > 2 × relative to linear excitation. We demonstrate these capabilities through molecular imaging of epithelial tissue, stem-cell-derived gastruloids, and living fruit fly embryos, including multicolor transcription-factor dynamics, optogenetic subcellular control, and single-mRNA tracking, all using standard glass-based mounting.

primary.title: Live-cell imaging of inter-organelle contacts using an integrated dimerization-dependent fluorescent protein reporter.
primary.abstract: Organelles communicate with each other by building membrane contact sites (MCSs) via specialized protein-protein and/or protein-membrane interactions. Conventional light microscopy cannot distinguish organelles connected by MCSs from those merely juxtaposed. In addition, organelle contacts are dynamic, yet only a limited number of tools are available to monitor MCSs in living cells. In this study, we developed a series of reporters based on dimerization-dependent fluorescent proteins (ddFP) to visualize, quantify and follow inter-organelle contacts. We first generated an integrated system specifically designed to study contacts between late endocytic compartments (late endosomes and lysosomes) and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). This system utilizes a single plasmid coding for the two complementary ddFP components: green A (GA) and green B (GB) targeted to the ER and late endosomes and lysosomes (LE/Lys), respectively. This construct enabled the generation of a stable reporter cell line suitable for semi-quantitative imaging. The ddFP reporter, which we called ddFP LELYS-ER, did not perturb endogenous LE/Lys-ER contacts in stable cells, and detected changes in the number of LE/Lys-ER contacts, for example, upon downregulation of the ER-resident VAP tether protein family, or under conditions of lysosomal damage. Moreover, live-cell imaging revealed that LE/Lys-ER contacts have distinct shapes, mobilities and lifetimes. Finally, using the same vector design, we generated two additional integrated reporter systems adapted to the study of contacts between the ER and the plasma membrane, and between the ER and mitochondria.

primary.title: Assessing cellular metabolic dynamics with two-photon NAD(P)H fluorescence polarization microscopy.
primary.abstract: Altered metabolism enables adaptive advantages for cancer cells, driving the need for improved methods for noninvasive long-term monitoring of cellular metabolism. Here, we present a fast live-cell NADH imaging method that provides a real-time measurement of the fractional level of unbound NADH and show that it is a robust indicator of a cell's metabolic status. The method, two-photon fluorescence polarization ratiometric microscopy (FPRM), is easy and inexpensive to implement and more than an order of magnitude faster than fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM), a common means of assessing bound and unbound NADH levels. We show that FPRM returns instrument-independent ratiometric parameters that correlate with the expected metabolic changes arising from pharmaceutical and environmental perturbations. By correlating FPRM-returned parameters with cell morphology and migration in two- and three-dimensional collagen matrices, we demonstrate the technique's versatility in typical bioengineered platforms used in cancer metabolism research.

primary.title: Lipid-induced Caveolin1 lipid droplet trafficking is associated with lipid droplet growth.
primary.abstract: Caveolae are 50 to 100 nm sized plasma membrane invaginations involved in cellular lipid uptake and lipid accumulation. Several caveolin1 and cavin1 mutations are associated with human lipodystrophy. Previous research identified caveolae proteins at lipid droplets, although their specific cellular function at lipid droplets is not understood. Here, we show that extracellular dietary lipids like oleic acid and cholesterol shift caveolae at the plasma membrane to highly spherical invaginations and induce the internalization of caveolin1. Within 3 h of lipid treatment, caveolin1 accumulates specifically to lipid droplets. Correlative fluorescence Focused Ion Beam - Scanning Electron Microscopy and split-APEX proteomics revealed that this localization occurs in the absence of intact caveolar vesicles but caveolin1 alone. Mechanistically, caveolin1 trafficking to lipid droplets is regulated by EHD2 at the plasma membrane, is dynamin independent, and proceeds via EEA1- and Rab5-positive endosomes within 1 h of oleic acid treatment. Lipid droplet accumulation of caveolin1 is independent of lysosomal activity. Functionally, caveolin1-enriched lipid droplets exhibit a significant increase in size, demonstrating that caveolin1 is critical for lipid droplet growth. Notably, the deletion of the central caveolin1 β-barrel (Cav1-F160X), a mutation identified in lipodystrophy patients, abolished caveolin1 lipid droplet trafficking and lipid droplet growth. Taken together, our results show that dietary lipids trigger caveolin1 internalization and accumulation at lipid droplets and a caveolin1-dependent lipid droplet growth, thereby providing an initial mechanistic basis for the lipodystrophic phenotype associated with caveolin1 mutations.

primary.title: Analysis of motor-based transport in primary cilia by dynamic mode decomposition of live-cell imaging data.
primary.abstract: Kinesin-3 motor proteins are increasingly recognized for their important roles in cilia. The mammalian kinesin-3 motor KIF13B moves bidirectionally in primary cilia and regulates ciliary content, but its relationship to the intraflagellar transport (IFT) machinery is unclear. Here, we combine quantitative live-cell imaging with a new kymograph analysis based on dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) to separate mobile from immobile protein populations in primary cilia. This approach simplifies extraction of molecular velocities from kymographs and improves directional analysis of molecular tracks using the Fourier and Radon transforms. Our novel analysis reveals that a KIF13B deletion mutant only retaining the motor domain and part of the forkhead-associated domain does not alter steady-state IFT velocity or frequency. However, when retrograde dynein-2 function is inhibited by ciliobrevin D or tanespimycin, both anterograde and retrograde IFT velocities decrease in parental cells, as expected, but remain unchanged in KIF13B mutant cells. Structured illumination, confocal and stimulated emission depletion (STED) microscopy further show that KIF13B localizes to the ciliary membrane and concentrates at the periciliary membrane region and the centriolar subdistal appendages, below the distal appendage marker FBF1. Our improved kymograph approach provides new insight into KIF13B ciliary function and simplifies the quantitative analysis of ciliary protein transport.

primary.title: SPIFFI enables single-shot super-resolution and multidimensional imaging.
primary.abstract: Fluorescence super-resolution microscopy has advanced optical imaging into the nanoscale regime, transforming biological and interdisciplinary research. However, wide-field super-resolution techniques often compromise temporal resolution, thereby limiting the capture of rapid and transient biological events in living systems. Here we introduce spatial polarization-induced fluorescence fluctuation imaging (SPIFFI), a multichannel polarimetric method for single-shot super-resolution imaging and six-dimensional information extraction. By leveraging the inherently smaller point spread function under polarized detection and capturing polarization-dependent spatial fluctuations across multiplexed channels, SPIFFI achieves instant resolution enhancement from a single exposure. This capability substantially enhances the feasibility of volumetric live-cell super-resolution imaging. Moreover, SPIFFI images can integrate seamlessly with existing fluctuation-based methods for further postprocessing and resolution improvement. We demonstrate the versatility of SPIFFI through experiments on both fixed and live cells, capturing rapid subcellular dynamics and enabling high-throughput, multidimensional imaging beyond the diffraction limit. SPIFFI thus offers a practical and robust platform for real-time super-resolution imaging in biological research.

primary.title: Broadband backscattering confocal microscopy enables label-free 3D live cell nanoscale sensitive imaging.
primary.abstract: Fluorescence microscopy is a cornerstone of biological research. However, fluorescent labeling is challenging in live cells and is constrained by photobleaching and phototoxicity. Label-free methods allow cells to be studied in their native state, but most techniques have poor contrast, lack 3D capability, rely on complex optics, or fail to provide structural information. We present here broadband backscattering confocal microscopy (BBCM), which employs a broadband supercontinuum laser and collects backscattered light in a confocal geometry using a photomultiplier tube. Broadband illumination averages out size-dependent oscillations that confound monochromatic backscattering. This eliminates blind spots and intensity ambiguities, allowing all scatterers to be visible, with the signal increasing approximately linearly with scatterer size. BBCM is easy to retrofit to standard confocal microscopes, requires no specialized optics, and is straightforward for nonspecialists. It enables high-contrast, label-free 3D imaging of live cells with size sensitivity to subcellular structures without employing custom optics or complex data processing.

primary.title: CelFDrive - multimodal deep learning-assisted microscopy for automated detection of rare events.
primary.abstract: The emergence of automated microscopy has enabled the collection of large datasets of rare biological events, accelerating discovery in biology. However, most existing methods cannot be readily integrated into microscopy setups or are limited to a single microscope type. We present CelFDrive, a software package that automatically detects rare events of interest and automates high-resolution three-dimensional imaging of target cells by integrating deep learning-assisted cell classification of auxiliary low-magnification fluorescence images. We show that CelFDrive reduced the mean time required to nominate a mitotic prophase candidate for high-resolution light-sheet imaging by over 30-fold relative to manual expert selection. This approach can be used to define the order of kinetochore assembly upon nuclear envelope breakdown. The trained CelFDrive detector demonstrated transferability by retaining mitotic cell detection capability in an independently generated dataset using a different cell line, DNA marker and imaging setup. As datasets grow and models improve, CelFDrive offers a clear path toward intelligent imaging systems that not only accelerate data collection, but also fundamentally enhance how biological questions are explored.

primary.title: Dual-modality photoacoustic and optical coherence tomography imaging simultaneously tracks transplanted stem cells and their viability.
primary.abstract: Monitoring transplanted cell viability in vivo, noninvasively remains a considerable challenge. By using multiwavelength photoacoustic microscopy powered by a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive contrast agent, we can relatively and semiquantitatively assess and longitudinally monitor the viability of human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal pigment epithelium (hiPSC-RPE) cells in vivo. The contrast agent comprises colloidal chain-like gold nanoparticle (CGNP) clusters conjugated with IR775c, a heptamethine cyanine dye that undergoes selective oxidative quenching under elevated ROS conditions associated with cellular death (CGNP-IR775c). Dual-wavelength photoacoustic microscopy at 620 and 775 nanometers provides self-calibrated ratiometric measurements that enable relative viability assessment, distinguishing healthy from nonviable cell populations. In vitro studies demonstrated that CGNP-IR775c exhibited biocompatibility and showed dose-dependent ROS sensitivity across physiologically relevant H2O2 concentrations. hiPSC-RPE cells labeled by CGNP-IR775c were subretinally transplanted into living rabbit eyes and longitudinally monitored for 2 weeks, showing that laser-induced oxidative stress produced measurable photoacoustic signal changes that were consistent with the viability status of the transplanted cells. The imaging technology developed here provides a practical solution for noninvasive, longitudinal, and semiquantitative assessment of the transplanted cell viability in vivo, and may contribute to ophthalmology cell-based therapy in both preclinical and clinical settings.

primary.title: Cellular-resolution three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) of neuronal population activity at 2-mm depth in the mammalian brain.
primary.abstract: Extending the depth reach of multiphoton microscopy for imaging neuronal population activity in the scattering mammalian brain is an 'exponentially hard' problem. Three-photon (3p) microscopy has enabled imaging of neuroactivity at depths up to ~1.2 mm in the mouse brain; however, the fundamental depth limit of 3p imaging, as set by the depth at which out-of-focus background fluorescence exceeds the in-focus fluorescence signal, is well beyond 2 mm. Reaching this fundamental depth limit in 3p imaging has been hampered by insufficient in-focus fluorescence signal. Here we demonstrate a three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) system that approaches this fundamental depth limit via systematic and principled optimization of the in-focus fluorescence signal. TrUDI matches the parameters of the excitation laser, the optical system, and the acquisition to linear and nonlinear limits for safe laser exposure while satisfying the spatiotemporal requirements of single-cell resolution calcium (Ca2+) imaging. TrUDI achieves a ~250-fold increase in detected fluorescence photon yield at the same laser power as in previous approaches thereby enabling in vivo cellular-resolution recordings of neuronal population activity within fields of view of ~230 × 230 µm2 at 8.6 Hz at tissue depths of up to ~2 mm in mouse cortex and hippocampus.

primary.title: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging.
primary.abstract: Direct monitoring the multifaceted intracellular microenvironment is fundamental for deciphering localized cellular behavior and function. However, performing nanoscale spatiotemporal sensing of the dynamic physiochemical environment within a live cell has remained challenging, mainly limited by the lack of robust, biocompatible method which satisfies the requirements for spatiotemporal resolution, sensitivity, multi-physical sensing capability and long-term viability. Here we present a super-resolution-based quantum biosensing approach, namely Super-resolution Multi-physical field Imaging with Deconvolution, implemented in our custom-built setup which integrates nitrogen vacancy center-based quantum sensing with structured illumination microscopy. This enables quantitative, super-resolved, and long-term tracking of intracellular physical fields, featuring spatial resolution of 136 nm, temporal resolution of 150 ms, and field of view of 180×180 μm2. We further perform super-resolution multimodal imaging in a live cell, revealing the spatially heterogeneous reactive oxygen species dynamics under external stimulation. Our work enables the dynamic assessment of localized physiochemical dynamics under super-resolution quantum biosensing.

primary.title: Space-time light-sheet microscopy.
primary.abstract: Light-sheet microscopy (LSM) has revolutionized bioimaging by delivering high-contrast volumetric resolution with minimal photodamage. Spatial wavefront shaping, used to generate lattice and Airy light-sheets, has been particularly effective in advancing LSM beyond the Rayleigh limit. Despite its broad adoption, most LSM implementations rely on rigid dual-objective geometries that complicate sample handling and impose a trade-off between imaging field of view (FoV) and axial resolution. Here, we introduce space-time light-sheet microscopy (ST-LSM), a single-objective strategy that exploits space-time (ST) correlations for the first time. ST-LSM goes beyond separate spatial or temporal modulation to jointly modulate the spatiotemporal spectral structure of a pulse. This enabled light-sheets with wavelength-scale thickness over millimeter-scale distances. When compared to state-of-the-art approaches, ST-LSM eliminates the dual-objective constraint, expands the sample-accessible volume by 25×, and increases the FoV by 10× without sacrificing sectioning resolution. We demonstrate the versatility of ST-LSM by using a single setup to image specimens across four orders of magnitude in size, from whole roots and developing embryos, down to mammalian cells with sub-cellular axial resolution. These results position ST-LSM as an accessible practical optical microscopy platform at a variety of biological scales, by translating space-time wavepacket physics into a practical imaging modality.

primary.title: Novel NaV1.6-Mitochondrial Complexes in Retinal Astrocyte Pockets Sequester GABA.
primary.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channels are best known for their capacity to generate and propagate electrical currents in neurons and muscle. Their expression in glial cells may also be of great importance given these cells' involvement in various disease processes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.6-enriched microdomain in mouse retinal astrocytes. Using super-resolution confocal microscopy, electrophysiology, and transcriptomic analyses, we show that NaV1.6 forms high-density clusters within intracellular compartments devoid of the calcium-binding protein, S100β, typically understood to distribute throughout the entire astrocyte. These NaV1.6 pockets are polarized, clustering only on the bilayer facing retinal ganglion cell neurons, and are packed with unusually large, anaplerotic, and relatively depolarized mitochondria that closely appose NaV1.6 puncta. These metabolic compartments also accumulate high levels of GABA. Together, our findings reveal a specialized NaV1.6-mitochondrial complex in retinal astrocytes that expands the functional repertoire of voltage-gated sodium channels beyond direct neuronal electrical excitability.

primary.title: Integrated two-photon and photoacoustic microscopy for single-cell neurometabolic imaging.
primary.abstract: Understanding how neuronal activity couples with local energy metabolism is fundamental to brain function. Oxygen exchange between individual neurons and red blood cells (RBCs) is central to this process, yet no existing method can simultaneously capture their dynamics at single-cell resolution in vivo. Here, we introduce integrated two-photon and photoacoustic microscopy (TPM-PAM), which enables real-time imaging of single-neuron calcium activity alongside oxygen release from individual RBCs in awake mice. In TPM-PAM, a transparent micro-ring resonator-based ultrasound sensor breaks the long-standing tradeoff between optical access and acoustic sensitivity, while dual-wavelength kymography simultaneously quantifies single-RBC oxygenation and flow to derive the oxygen release rate. Incorporating nonlinear optical manipulation of the neurovascular unit with cellular precision, TPM-PAM reveals distinct neurometabolic responses to whisker stimulation, single-capillary occlusion, and single-neuron stimulation. This work establishes a powerful platform for dissecting neurometabolic coupling at the cellular scale and understanding oxygen-metabolic regulation in brain health and disease.

primary.title: Submicromolar imaging of intrinsic chromophores by two-photon photothermal microscopy captures mitochondrial response to chemotherapy.
primary.abstract: Intracellular chromophores {e.g., NADH [reduced form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (oxidized form)] and FAD (flavin adenine dinucleotide)} play a central role in regulation of cellular metabolism. Although autofluorescence has been extensively used for label-free mapping of chromophores inside a cell, its sensitivity and molecular specificity are constrained by the low quantum yield and the fluorescence spectral overlap. Here, we address these challenges by using a photothermal approach to measure the optical absorption of chromophores rather than its autofluorescence. Our two-photon photothermal (2PPT) microscope exploits localized thermal transients generated through two-photon absorption, enabling detection of chromophore-specific signatures beyond the reach of autofluorescence. We demonstrate submicromolar limits of detection for the metabolic coenzymes NADH and FAD of 0.87 and 0.99 μM, respectively. Such high sensitivity enables differentiating the influence of mitochondrial shapes on metabolism. 2PPT can identify the biomolecular source of contrast from cellular mitochondria in a label-free manner on the basis of spectroscopy. 2PPT microscopy is used to study metabolic alterations of mitochondria in cancer under chemotherapy at the single-organelle level.

Future studies should aim to integrate 2PPT with complementary imaging modalities and develop analytical models to correlate photothermal signatures with metabolic flux.

primary.title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning.
primary.abstract: Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

primary.title: Coincidence detection in aspiny interneuron dendrites.
primary.abstract: Recent evidence for long-term potentiation (LTP) at glutamatergic synapses on GABAergic interneurons calls for close attention to the sub-cellular phenomena that underlie the induction of plasticity in aspiny dendrites. Neurogliaform interneurons exhibit large NMDA receptor-mediated currents, Hebbian LTP and supralinear summation of glutamatergic signals converging on dendritic compartments. Dendritic supralinearity in interneurons does not require sodium channels. Here we investigate the principles governing supralinear synaptic integration and its interaction with backpropagating action potentials in the synaptic plasticity context. We developed a biophysically realistic, multi-compartmental model of a murine (Mus musculus, male and female) hippocampal neurogliaform interneuron, with dendritic architecture and ion channel densities tuned to match ex vivo recordings. The interaction between synaptic inputs and action potentials was tested with patch-clamp electrophysiology and two-photon imaging of dendritic calcium-dependent fluorescence transients. Whether simulated glutamatergic excitatory postsynaptic potentials are clustered on a dendritic fragment or dispersed across the entire arbor, they summate supralinearly as assessed from the calculated somatic voltage response. Clustered inputs induce more pronounced local depolarizations and calcium transients than dispersed inputs. Action potentials generated at the soma backpropagate throughout the dendritic arbor but are attenuated at branch points. Coincident synaptic input and backpropagating action potentials relieve this attenuation, further enhance dendritic depolarizations, and greatly potentiate calcium influx via NMDA receptors. Despite differences in dendritic anatomy and in the roles of sodium channels, the interplay of orthodromic and antidromic voltage propagation and resultant calcium signal amplification exhibits remarkable similarities between neurogliaform interneurons and principal cells.Significance Statement Neurogliaform interneurons are key regulators of brain circuit activity, yet the dendritic mechanisms that enable these inhibitory cells to undergo synaptic plasticity remain poorly understood. Combining biophysically realistic computer modeling with electrophysiology and two-photon calcium imaging, we show that coincident synaptic input and backpropagating action potentials strongly amplify dendritic depolarization and calcium influx in these interneurons. Although their dendrites lack spines and do not rely on sodium-channel-dependent dendritic spikes, neurogliaform interneurons nonetheless use computational principles remarkably similar to those of excitatory principal neurons. These findings advance the understanding of how inhibitory circuits support learning-related plasticity and may provide foundational insight into disorders such as epilepsy and schizophrenia, in which abnormal dendritic signalling and inhibitory dysfunction are implicated.

primary.title: Incomplete synaptic vesicle priming functionally disconnects CA1 pyramidal cells.
primary.abstract: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid-releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.

primary.title: 53BP1 as a cofactor in the activation of the p53-family transcriptional program: A correlative multimodal microscopy approach.
primary.abstract: Understanding how molecular mechanisms regulate cell function in tissues requires approaches that link phenotypes to mechanisms across different spatial scales. Here, we present automated multimodal multiplexed microscopy for image cytometry (A.M3.I.CO), a correlative imaging platform that combines multiscale resolution, from millimeters to nanometers, with automated workflows for high-throughput phenotypic profiling and targeted single-molecule analysis in situ. Applying A.M3.I.CO, we observed that 53BP1 is recruited at transcribed p53 target genes independently of the activating stimulus, providing evidence for the formation of a putative complex between 53BP1, p53, and the basal transcription machinery in single cells, as also supported by in vivo observations in tumor models. Extending our measurements to p63 and p73, we found that 53BP1 localized at p63- and p73-targeted transcription sites, suggesting a broader role in participating in p53 family-dependent transcription. These findings indicate an additional genome-surveillance pathway in transcriptional control regulating diverse cellular functions while establishing A.M3.I.CO as a platform for spatially resolved functional analysis.

primary.title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics.
primary.abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

primary.title: Volume electron microscopy reveals oligodendrocyte axon selection patterns and spatial assembly of myelin and nodes.
primary.abstract: Oligodendrocytes myelinate multiple axons, requiring single cells to coordinate target selection, sheath growth, and node formation across complex cortical geometry. We combined serial block-face electron microscopy, complete segmentation, and three-dimensional reconstruction to analyze early-myelinating oligodendrocytes in the somatosensory cortex of a postnatal day 14 rat at single-cell and nanoscale resolution. Individual oligodendrocytes initiated myelination across all contacted axons, while early ensheathment decreased with increasing process distance from the soma. Each oligodendrocyte also contacted axons within a restricted caliber range, independently of wrapping progression. At prospective nodes of Ranvier, transient cytoplasmic projections extended into axonal domains from adjacent oligodendrocytes and converged near presumptive paranodes. These observations support a structural model in which oligodendrocyte geometry, cell-specific axon selection, and intercellular interactions jointly organize early cortical myelination and nodal assembly, providing testable hypotheses for developmental myelination and repair after demyelination.

primary.title: FLIM Playground: An interactive, end-to-end graphical user interface for analyzing single cells with fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy.
primary.abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) is sensitive to molecular environments and enables high-resolution mapping of cellular heterogeneity. Yet, the journey from raw photon decays to biological insight remains fragmented by multi-step data extraction and siloed analyses, creating burdens for experts and non-experts alike. This work presents FLIM Playground, the first interactive graphical platform that unifies single-cell FLIM workflows. Modularly designed to encompass data extraction (if desired) and data analysis, FLIM Playground can check field-of-view metadata, calibrate and extract fluorescence lifetime features per region of interest along with morphology and texture features across channels, merge multiple datasets, and provide real-time visual analytic modules. Lifetime extraction was validated against commercial software and published results, and both data extraction and analysis were demonstrated on a FLIM dataset of cancer cell lines. By adopting best practices and offering interactivity, FLIM Playground promotes reproducibility, allows for expansion to new imaging modalities, and accelerates hypothesis-driven discovery.

primary.title: Btbd11 regulates glutamatergic synapse organization in GABAergic inhibitory interneurons.
primary.abstract: The mechanisms that underlie glutamatergic synapse organization and function in GABAergic inhibitory interneurons (INs) are not well described, despite evidence that impaired glutamatergic excitation of INs is implicated in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia and anxiety. Glutamatergic synapses received by INs have unique basal transmission properties and exhibit distinct synaptic plasticity compared to those received by excitatory neurons, likely due to cell-type specific differences in postsynaptic density (PSD) composition and maintenance mechanisms. In the present study, we show that the interneuron-specific protein Btbd11 regulates excitatory synapse transmission in mixed-sex primary cultured rat and mouse hippocampal interneurons through promotion of phase separation and support of postsynaptic nanoarchitecture. Btbd11 forms a phase separated protein complex with Psd-95 and TARPγ2 and impacts the stability of TARPγ2 and GluA1 within glutamatergic IN synapses in an expression- and phase separation-dependent manner. Using super resolution imaging, we show that Btbd11 displays nanoscale clustering properties within IN synapses that correlate with Psd-95 nanostructure. Furthermore, genetic deletion of Btbd11 decreases PSD protein expression, reduces synapse size, and disrupts Psd-95 nanocluster organization. These effects manifest as a drastic reduction in glutamatergic synaptic transmission onto INs when Btbd11 is deleted. Together, these data provide insights into a novel cell type-specific synaptic regulatory mechanism in an understudied synapse population.Significance Statement Although glutamatergic excitation of GABAergic inhibitory interneurons (INs) is essential for maintenance of balanced signaling in the brain and dysregulation has been linked to neuropsychiatric disorders, the molecular mechanisms underlying IN-specific glutamatergic transmission are not well characterized. Using protein modeling, molecular biology, live-cell and super-resolution imaging, we describe a unique mechanism of glutamatergic synapse organization in INs by Btbd11, an IN-specific synaptic protein. Btbd11 promotes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) and regulates PSD protein mobility, the abundance of key synaptic proteins, and nanoscale synaptic organization. Collectively, this is critical for glutamatergic synaptic transmission within INs. Understanding Btbd11's role at the synapse highlights the importance of synaptic LLPS, providing insight into the regulatory mechanisms in an understudied synapse with psychiatric disease relevance.

primary.title: Structural basis for the selective inhibition of the PI3KC3-C2 complex by Rubicon in endolysosome maturation and mitophagy.
primary.abstract: Rubicon is a negative regulator of autophagy and the endolysosomal network (ELN) and an antagonist of the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex II (PI3KC3-C2). Inhibition of Rubicon is considered a potential means to therapeutically upregulate autophagy and the ELN to treat Parkinson's disease and other conditions characterized by autophagic and ELN dysfunction. Rubicon is specific for the UV radiation resistance-associated gene protein (UVRAG)-containing PI3KC3-C2 over the purely autophagic ATG14-containing PI3KC3-C1 complex. Here, we determined the high-resolution cryoelectron microscopy structure of PI3KC3-C2 in complex with the PI3KC3-binding domain of Rubicon and compared it to cryo-EM structures of unbound PI3KC3-C2 and PI3KC3-C1. Rubicon binds directly to PI3KC3-C2 only via the BARA domain of the BECN1 subunit, which is common to both C1 and C2. The selectivity of Rubicon for the PI3KC3-C2 complex over the PI3KC3-C1 complex is attributed to a conformation of the BECN1BARA domain induced by UVRAG, rather than to direct contact with UVRAG or direct antagonism by the ATG14 subunit of PI3KC3-C1. Targeted disruption of the Rubicon:PI3K3-C2 structural interface by site-directed mutations enhances mitophagic activity in human epithelial cells to levels comparable to those observed in Rubicon knockout cells. Similarly, disruption of the interaction in Rubicon-overexpressing hippocampal neurons restored lysosomal flux to wild-type levels. These data show that suppressing the function of PI3K3-C2 can fully account for the negative regulatory effects of Rubicon in the autophagy and ELN pathways.

primary.title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions.
primary.abstract: Monitoring large-scale neuronal activity in deep brain circuits is crucial for understanding the principles of brain function. However, existing large-scale cellular-resolution imaging techniques are limited in imaging depth and cannot monitor activity in areas deeper than the cortex in the intact brain. To address this challenge, we developed a Large Imaging Field of view Three-photon (LIFT) microscope with a FOV of  > 3 mm2. LIFT combines high-numerical-aperture optimized sampling, using a custom scanning module, with deep learning-based denoising, to enable population imaging in subcortical brain regions of mice and deep cortical regions of rats. We demonstrate calcium imaging in the intact mouse brain from more than 1500 cells across CA1, the surrounding white matter, and adjacent deep layers of the cortex, and show population imaging with high SNR at a depth of 1.2 mm in the rat cortex. The LIFT microscope offers versatility in imaging scale and rate and was built entirely from off-the-shelf components.

primary.title: MIMAS: An open-source microlens-array miniature microscope for accessible large-field cortical imaging in freely behaving mice.
primary.abstract: Large-scale cortical dynamics during natural behavior are difficult to measure because head-mounted imaging systems must balance field of view, spatial resolution, weight, and optical complexity. Existing wide-field miniature microscopes often rely on compound or custom-corrected optical assemblies, which increase device complexity and limit accessibility for laboratories without specialized optics expertise. Here, we present the Miniature Integrated Microlens Array System (MIMAS), an open-source head-mounted fluorescence microscope that replaces conventional multi-element optics with a 4 × 5 microlens array as its sole imaging element. By combining modular subfield acquisition with computational registration and stitching, MIMAS achieves cellular-resolution imaging across an approximately 4 × 4.5 mm2 field of view while weighing only 2.31 g. In freely behaving mice with sparse labeling of layer 2/3 cortical neurons, MIMAS enabled simultaneous calcium imaging across multiple dorsal cortical regions, with signals extracted from thousands of neurons. This broad sampling captured distributed cortical activity related to locomotor state and sparse position-modulated responses during open-field exploration without detectable disruption of locomotion or loss of signal quality over 30 min of recording. Beyond neuronal imaging, MIMAS also supported wide-field vascular imaging and resolved vessel caliber-dependent hemodynamic responses to isoflurane. These results establish MIMAS as a lightweight, accessible, and versatile platform for large-scale fluorescence imaging in freely behaving mice and demonstrate an alternative strategy for wide-field cortical imaging that lowers the optical complexity barrier for individual laboratories.

primary.title: Deep learning-enhanced single-shot triorganelle STED-FLIM imaging of lipid dynamics in living cells.
primary.abstract: Lipid homeostasis is orchestrated by rapid exchange and remodeling across the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), lipid droplets (LDs), and mitochondria. However, live-cell visualization of this triorganelle network remains limited by subdiffraction structures, multiplexed labeling burden, and the ambiguity of intensity-only readouts. Here, we introduce a single-shot stimulated emission depletion-fluorescence lifetime imaging (STED-FLIM) workflow that combines Nile Red analogs with deep learning-based demultiplexing to generate compartment-resolved maps of lipid-organelle organization and dynamics. By combining the STED-resolved nanoscale ultrastructure with lifetime-encoded microenvironmental contrast, our approach separates ER, LDs, and mitochondria from a single acquisition and enables automated tricompartment quantification using a lightweight VGG16-UNet segmentation model. This platform captures coordinated remodeling across the ER-LD-mitochondria axis during lipid stress, including ferroptosis- and apoptosis-associated transitions, while simultaneously reporting nanoscale organization and microenvironmental shifts. Together, this strategy provides a practical route to high-spatiotemporal-resolution, lifetime-encoded multiorganelle lipid imaging in living cells.
